source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: All titles are inside public verse 1. Psalms 108, 140, 142 bind one separate title record plus Hebrew verse 2 to public verse 1; following labels are offset by one. Other selected labels match. All 717 original source records bind exactly once, including every note; no source record is partitioned in this batch.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Preserves invocation and outward witness as separate imperatives.
verses.before: Give thanks to the LORD, call upon his name; reveal his deeds among the peoples!
verses.after: Give thanks to the LORD; call on his name. Make his deeds known among the peoples.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give thanks to the LORD, call upon his name; make known his deeds among the peoples!

verses.rationale: Retains both musical verbs and the scope of wonders.
verses.before: Sing to him, sing praises to him; tell of all his wondrous works!
verses.after: Sing to him; make music for him. Tell of all his wonders.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sing to him, sing praises to him; tell of all his wondrous works!

verses.rationale: Locates boasting in the name and joy in seekers' hearts.
verses.before: Glory in his holy name; let the hearts of people who seek the LORD rejoice!
verses.after: Take pride in his holy name. Let those who seek the LORD rejoice in their hearts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Glory in his holy name; let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice!

verses.rationale: Renders seeking the face as seeking presence, retaining repetition.
verses.before: Seek the LORD and his strength; seek his face continually!
verses.after: Seek the LORD and his strength; seek his presence always.
verses.tsw_comparator: Seek the LORD and his strength; seek his face continually!

verses.rationale: Keeps three objects of remembrance and the spoken judgments.
verses.before: Remember the wondrous works that he has done, his miracles and the judgments he has spoken,
verses.after: Remember the wonders he has done, his signs and the judgments he has spoken,
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember the wondrous works that he has done, his miracles and the judgments he has spoken,

verses.rationale: Preserves the two ancestral addresses and servant/chosen distinction.
verses.before: O offspring of Abraham his servant, children of Jacob, his chosen ones!
verses.after: you offspring of Abraham his servant, you children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
verses.tsw_comparator: O offspring of Abraham his servant, children of Jacob, his chosen ones!

verses.rationale: Retains identification and worldwide judgment.
verses.before: He is the LORD our God; his judgments are in all the earth.
verses.after: He is the LORD our God; his judgments reach throughout the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: He is the LORD our God; his judgments are in all the earth.

verses.rationale: Keeps commanded word, covenant, and thousand-generation horizon.
verses.before: He remembers his covenant forever, the word that he commanded, for a thousand generations,
verses.after: He remembers his covenant forever, the word he commanded for a thousand generations,
verses.tsw_comparator: He remembers his covenant forever, the word that he commanded, for a thousand generations,

verses.rationale: Carries the preceding syntax through the two ancestors.
verses.before: the covenant that he made with Abraham, his sworn promise to Isaac,
verses.after: the covenant he made with Abraham, the oath he swore to Isaac.
verses.tsw_comparator: the covenant that he made with Abraham, his sworn promise to Isaac,

verses.rationale: Preserves parallel names and decree/covenant terminology.
verses.before: which he confirmed to Jacob as a statute, to Israel as an everlasting covenant,
verses.after: He established it for Jacob as a decree, for Israel as an everlasting covenant,
verses.tsw_comparator: which he confirmed to Jacob as a statute, to Israel as an everlasting covenant,

verses.rationale: Retains gift, named land, and measured inheritance image.
verses.before: saying, “To you I will give the land of Canaan as your portion for an inheritance.”
verses.after: saying, “I will give you the land of Canaan as your allotted inheritance.”
verses.tsw_comparator: saying, “To you I will give the land of Canaan as your portion for an inheritance.”

verses.rationale: Preserves intensified smallness and resident-alien status.
verses.before: When they were few in number, of little account, and sojourners in it,
verses.after: When they were few in number, very few, and living there as foreigners,
verses.tsw_comparator: When they were few in number, of little account, and sojourners in it,

verses.rationale: Keeps both forms of movement without supplying destinations.
verses.before: wandering from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people,
verses.after: they wandered from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people.
verses.tsw_comparator: wandering from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people,

verses.rationale: Retains protective action and rebuked rulers.
verses.before: he allowed no one to oppress them; he rebuked kings on their account,
verses.after: He let no one oppress them; for their sake he rebuked kings:
verses.tsw_comparator: he allowed no one to oppress them; he rebuked kings on their account,

verses.rationale: Keeps plural anointed ones and prophetic designation.
verses.before: saying, “Do not touch my anointed ones; do my prophets no harm.”
verses.after: “Do not touch my anointed ones; do not harm my prophets.”
verses.tsw_comparator: saying, “Do not touch my anointed ones; do my prophets no harm.”

verses.rationale: Preserves divine agency and the bread-as-staff image.
verses.before: When he summoned a famine on the land and broke all supply of bread,
verses.after: He called a famine down on the land and broke every staff of bread that sustained them.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he summoned a famine on the land and broke all supply of bread,

verses.rationale: Makes Joseph's enslavement explicit without erasing providential framing.
verses.before: he sent a man before them— Joseph, sold as a slave.
verses.after: He sent a man ahead of them: Joseph, who was sold as a slave.
verses.tsw_comparator: he sent a man before them— Joseph, sold as a slave.

verses.rationale: Follows the singular read form of foot and physical restraint idiom.
verses.before: His feet were hurt with fetters; his neck was put in a collar of iron;
verses.after: They hurt his foot with shackles; his neck was put in iron,
verses.tsw_comparator: His feet were hurt with fetters; his neck was put in a collar of iron;

verses.rationale: Leaves the antecedent of his word open and retains testing.
verses.before: until what he had said happened, the word of the LORD tested him.
verses.after: until his word came true. The LORD’s utterance tested him.
verses.tsw_comparator: until what he had said came to pass, the word of the LORD tested him.

verses.rationale: Retains the parallel descriptions of release.
verses.before: The king sent and released him; the ruler of the peoples set him free;
verses.after: The king sent for him and set him free; the ruler of peoples released him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king sent and released him; the ruler of the peoples set him free;

verses.rationale: Keeps household and possessions as distinct jurisdictions.
verses.before: he made him lord of his house and ruler of all his possessions,
verses.after: He made him master of his household and ruler over all he owned,
verses.tsw_comparator: he made him lord of his house and ruler of all his possessions,

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult binding verb rather than replacing it with instruction.
verses.before: to bind his princes at his pleasure and to teach his elders wisdom.
verses.after: to bind his princes as he wished and teach his elders wisdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: to bind his princes at his pleasure and to teach his elders wisdom.

verses.rationale: Maintains ancestral parallelism and ancient name Ham.
verses.before: Then Israel came to Egypt; Jacob sojourned in the land of Ham.
verses.after: Then Israel came to Egypt; Jacob lived as a foreigner in the land of Ham.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Israel came to Egypt; Jacob sojourned in the land of Ham.

verses.rationale: Clarifies divine subject without changing fertility and strength claims.
verses.before: And the LORD made his people very fruitful and made them stronger than their foes.
verses.after: God made his people very fruitful and stronger than their foes.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD made his people very fruitful and made them stronger than their foes.

verses.rationale: Preserves the troubling divine agency and both hostile actions.
verses.before: He turned their hearts to hate his people, to deal craftily with his servants.
verses.after: He turned their hearts to hate his people, to deal deceitfully with his servants.
verses.tsw_comparator: He turned their hearts to hate his people, to deal craftily with his servants.

verses.rationale: Keeps the differentiated descriptions of Moses and Aaron.
verses.before: He sent Moses his servant, and Aaron, whom he had chosen.
verses.after: He sent Moses his servant and Aaron, whom he had chosen.
verses.tsw_comparator: He sent Moses his servant, and Aaron, whom he had chosen.

verses.rationale: Retains plural agents and the parallel location.
verses.before: They performed his signs among them and miracles in the land of Ham.
verses.after: They performed his signs among them, his wonders in the land of Ham.
verses.tsw_comparator: They performed his signs among them and miracles in the land of Ham.

verses.rationale: Preserves the negative and leaves the plural subject unexpanded.
verses.before: He sent darkness, and made the land dark; they did not rebel against his words.
verses.after: He sent darkness, and it grew dark; they did not rebel against his word.
verses.tsw_comparator: He sent darkness, and made the land dark; they did not rebel against his words.

verses.rationale: Keeps the direct divine actions and their victims.
verses.before: He turned their waters into blood and caused their fish to die.
verses.after: He turned their waters into blood and killed their fish.
verses.tsw_comparator: He turned their waters into blood and caused their fish to die.

verses.rationale: Retains royal chambers and plural kings.
verses.before: Their land swarmed with frogs, even in the chambers of their kings.
verses.after: Their land swarmed with frogs, even in the chambers of their kings.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their land swarmed with frogs, even in the chambers of their kings.

verses.rationale: Preserves speech as cause and two pests.
verses.before: He spoke, and there came swarms of flies, and gnats throughout their country.
verses.after: He spoke, and swarms of flies came, and gnats throughout their territory.
verses.tsw_comparator: He spoke, and there came swarms of flies, and gnats throughout their country.

verses.rationale: Retains rain's reversal and fire imagery.
verses.before: He gave them hail for rain, and flaming fire in their land.
verses.after: He gave them hail in place of rain, flaming fire across their land.
verses.tsw_comparator: He gave them hail for rain, and flaming fire in their land.

verses.rationale: Keeps both named crops and wider tree destruction.
verses.before: He struck down their vines and fig trees, and shattered the trees of their country.
verses.after: He struck their vines and fig trees and shattered the trees of their territory.
verses.tsw_comparator: He struck down their vines and fig trees, and shattered the trees of their country.

verses.rationale: Retains the second locust designation and uncountable number.
verses.before: He spoke, and the locusts came, young locusts without number,
verses.after: He spoke, and locusts came, devouring locusts beyond counting.
verses.tsw_comparator: He spoke, and the locusts came, young locusts without number,

verses.rationale: Preserves the two comprehensive descriptions of consumption.
verses.before: which devoured all the vegetation in their land and ate up the fruit of their ground.
verses.after: They ate every plant in their land and consumed the produce of their ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: which devoured all the vegetation in their land and ate up the fruit of their ground.

verses.rationale: Keeps firstborn deaths and the reproductive-strength image.
verses.before: He struck down all the firstborn in their land, the firstfruits of all their strength.
verses.after: He struck every firstborn in their land, the first yield of all their strength.
verses.tsw_comparator: He struck down all the firstborn in their land, the firstfruits of all their strength.

verses.rationale: Retains possessions and the absence of stumbling.
verses.before: Then he brought out Israel with silver and gold, and there was none among his tribes who stumbled.
verses.after: He brought his people out with silver and gold; no one among his tribes stumbled.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he brought out Israel with silver and gold, and there was none among his tribes who stumbled.

verses.rationale: Preserves Egypt's personification and the stated reason for relief.
verses.before: Egypt was glad when they departed, for dread of them had fallen upon it.
verses.after: Egypt was glad when they left, for dread of them had fallen on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Egypt was glad when they departed, for dread of them had fallen upon it.

verses.rationale: Keeps covering and illumination distinct.
verses.before: He spread a cloud for a covering, and fire to give light by night.
verses.after: He spread a cloud as a covering and fire to give light at night.
verses.tsw_comparator: He spread a cloud for a covering, and fire to give light by night.

verses.rationale: Renders the singular collective request in natural English.
verses.before: They asked, and he brought quail, and gave them bread from heaven in abundance.
verses.after: His people asked, and he brought quail; he satisfied them with bread from heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: They asked, and he brought quail, and gave them bread from heaven in abundance.

verses.rationale: Preserves opening, gushing, and river in arid ground.
verses.before: He opened the rock, and water gushed out; it flowed through the desert like a river.
verses.after: He opened a rock, and water gushed out; it flowed through dry places like a river.
verses.tsw_comparator: He opened the rock, and water gushed out; it flowed through the desert like a river.

verses.rationale: Keeps remembrance tied to both promise and servant.
verses.before: For he remembered his holy promise, and Abraham his servant.
verses.after: For he remembered his holy word and Abraham his servant.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he remembered his holy promise, and Abraham his servant.

verses.rationale: Retains parallel people/chosen and audible rejoicing.
verses.before: So he brought his people out with joy, his chosen ones with singing.
verses.after: He brought his people out with joy, his chosen ones with shouts of celebration.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he brought his people out with joy, his chosen ones with singing.

verses.rationale: Preserves transfer of land and others' labor without softening conquest.
verses.before: And he gave them the lands of the nations, and they took possession of the fruit of the peoples’ labor,
verses.after: He gave them the lands of nations; they inherited what other peoples had labored for,
verses.tsw_comparator: And he gave them the lands of the nations, and they took possession of the fruit of the peoples’ labor,

verses.rationale: Retains the purpose clause, two instruction terms, and short divine name.
verses.before: that they might keep his statutes and observe his laws. Praise the LORD!
verses.after: so that they would keep his decrees and guard his instructions. Praise YAH!
verses.tsw_comparator: that they might keep his statutes and observe his laws. Praise the LORD!

verses.rationale: Preserves both divine-name forms and the recurring thanksgiving formula.
verses.before: Praise the LORD! Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good, for his steadfast love endures forever!
verses.after: Praise YAH! Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Praise the LORD! Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good, for his steadfast love endures forever!

verses.rationale: Keeps the rhetorical question and totality of praise.
verses.before: Who can utter the mighty deeds of the LORD, or declare all his praise?
verses.after: Who can tell all the LORD’s mighty deeds or make all his praise heard?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who can utter the mighty deeds of the LORD, or declare all his praise?

verses.rationale: Retains justice, enacted righteousness, and continual practice.
verses.before: Blessed are people who keep justice, who do righteousness at all times!
verses.after: Happy are those who keep justice, who do what is right at every moment.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed are those who keep justice, who do righteousness at all times!

verses.rationale: Preserves singular plea within communal favor.
verses.before: Remember me, O LORD, when you show favor to your people; help me when you save them,
verses.after: Remember me, LORD, when you show favor to your people; come to my aid when you save them,
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember me, O LORD, when you show favor to your people; help me when you save them,

verses.rationale: Keeps the three desired participations and inheritance-community sense.
verses.before: that I may see the good of your chosen ones, that I may rejoice in the gladness of your nation, that I may glory with your inheritance.
verses.after: so I may see your chosen ones prosper, rejoice in your nation’s joy, and share the pride of your own people.
verses.tsw_comparator: that I may see the good of your chosen ones, that I may rejoice in the gladness of your nation, that I may glory with your inheritance.

verses.rationale: Retains communal confession with ancestral continuity and three verbs.
verses.before: Both we and our ancestors have sinned; we have committed iniquity; we have done wickedness.
verses.after: We have sinned, just as our ancestors did; we have done wrong; we have acted wickedly.
verses.tsw_comparator: Both we and our ancestors have sinned; we have committed iniquity; we have done wickedness.

verses.rationale: Preserves failure of understanding and memory and the sea's Hebrew name.
verses.before: Our ancestors in Egypt did not consider your wonders; they did not remember the abundance of your steadfast love, but rebelled by the sea, at the Red Sea.
verses.after: Our ancestors in Egypt did not grasp your wonders or remember your abundant faithful love. They rebelled by the sea, the Sea of Reeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: Our ancestors in Egypt did not consider your wonders; they did not remember the abundance of your steadfast love, but rebelled by the sea, at the Red Sea.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two stated purposes rather than supplying merit.
verses.before: Yet he saved them for his name’s sake, that he might reveal his mighty power.
verses.after: Yet he saved them for his name’s sake, to make his might known.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet he saved them for his name’s sake, that he might make known his mighty power.

verses.rationale: Retains rebuke and the surprising depths/desert comparison.
verses.before: He rebuked the Red Sea, and it became dry, and he led them through the deep as through a desert.
verses.after: He rebuked the Sea of Reeds, and it dried up; he led them through the depths as through a desert.
verses.tsw_comparator: He rebuked the Red Sea, and it became dry, and he led them through the deep as through a desert.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated hand imagery and redemption vocabulary.
verses.before: So he saved them from the hand of the one who hated them and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.
verses.after: He saved them from the hand of those who hated them and redeemed them from the enemy’s hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he saved them from the hand of the one who hated them and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.

verses.rationale: Retains complete loss of the pursuers.
verses.before: And the waters covered their adversaries; not one of them was left.
verses.after: The waters covered their foes; not one of them was left.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the waters covered their adversaries; not one of them was left.

verses.rationale: Keeps belief and song as the immediate response.
verses.before: Then they believed his words; they sang his praise.
verses.after: Then they believed his words and sang his praise.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they believed his words; they sang his praise.

verses.rationale: Preserves the rapid reversal and refusal to wait.
verses.before: But they soon forgot his works; they did not wait for his counsel.
verses.after: But they quickly forgot what he had done; they would not wait for his counsel.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they soon forgot his works; they did not wait for his counsel.

verses.rationale: Keeps intensified appetite and testing God.
verses.before: But they had a craving in the wilderness and tested God in the desert.
verses.after: They were seized by craving in the wilderness and put God to the test in the wasteland.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they had a craving in the wilderness and tested God in the desert.

verses.rationale: Takes leanness as bodily affliction without spiritualizing the harm.
verses.before: He gave them what they asked, but sent a wasting disease among them.
verses.after: He gave them what they asked for but sent wasting into their bodies.
verses.tsw_comparator: He gave them what they asked, but sent a wasting disease among them.

verses.rationale: Retains both targets and Aaron's designation.
verses.before: When men in the camp were jealous of Moses and Aaron, the holy one of the LORD,
verses.after: In the camp they grew jealous of Moses and of Aaron, the LORD’s holy one.
verses.tsw_comparator: When men in the camp were jealous of Moses and Aaron, the holy one of the LORD,

verses.rationale: Preserves the two named rebels and the fate of the company.
verses.before: the earth opened and swallowed Dathan, and covered the company of Abiram.
verses.after: The earth opened and swallowed Dathan; it closed over Abiram’s company.
verses.tsw_comparator: the earth opened and swallowed Dathan, and covered the company of Abiram.

verses.rationale: Keeps the parallel destructive fire clauses.
verses.before: Fire also broke out in their company; the flame burned up the wicked.
verses.after: Fire blazed through their company; flames consumed the wicked.
verses.tsw_comparator: Fire also broke out in their company; the flame burned up the wicked.

verses.rationale: Retains location, animal image, and manufacture.
verses.before: They made a calf in Horeb and worshiped a metal image.
verses.after: At Horeb they made a calf and bowed down to an image cast from metal.
verses.tsw_comparator: They made a calf in Horeb and worshiped a metal image.

verses.rationale: Follows their glory and preserves the diminishing grass-eating image.
verses.before: They exchanged their glory for the image of an ox that eats grass.
verses.after: They exchanged their glory for the likeness of an ox that eats grass.
verses.tsw_comparator: They exchanged their glory for the image of an ox that eats grass.

verses.rationale: Carries the accusation into the following catalogue.
verses.before: They forgot God, their Savior, who had done great things in Egypt,
verses.after: They forgot God their savior, who had done great things in Egypt,
verses.tsw_comparator: They forgot God, their Savior, who had done great things in Egypt,

verses.rationale: Retains both ancient locations and the fearful quality of the deeds.
verses.before: wondrous works in the land of Ham, and awesome deeds by the Red Sea.
verses.after: wonders in the land of Ham, terrifying deeds at the Sea of Reeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: wondrous works in the land of Ham, and awesome deeds by the Red Sea.

verses.rationale: Keeps the threatened destruction and defensive-breach intercession image.
verses.before: So he said he would destroy them— had not Moses, his chosen one, stood in the breach before him, to turn away his wrath from destroying them.
verses.after: He said he would destroy them, had Moses his chosen one not stood in the breach before him to turn his fury away from destroying them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore he said he would destroy them— had not Moses, his chosen one, stood in the breach before him, to turn away his wrath from destroying them.

verses.rationale: Preserves contempt for a good land and disbelief.
verses.before: Then they despised the pleasant land, having no faith in his promise.
verses.after: They despised the desirable land and did not believe his word.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they despised the pleasant land, having no faith in his promise.

verses.rationale: Keeps private setting and refusal to hear.
verses.before: They murmured in their tents, and did not obey the voice of the LORD.
verses.after: They grumbled in their tents and would not listen to the LORD’s voice.
verses.tsw_comparator: They murmured in their tents, and did not obey the voice of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Makes oath gesture intelligible while preserving the falling judgment.
verses.before: So he raised his hand against them, to make them fall in the wilderness,
verses.after: So he raised his hand in an oath against them: he would make them fall in the wilderness,
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore he raised his hand against them, to make them fall in the wilderness,

verses.rationale: Retains falling as well as scattering, without silently emending the verb.
verses.before: and to scatter their offspring among the nations, dispersing them throughout the lands.
verses.after: make their offspring fall among the nations, and scatter them across the lands.
verses.tsw_comparator: and to scatter their offspring among the nations, dispersing them throughout the lands.

verses.rationale: Leaves the referent of the dead open and retains cultic attachment.
verses.before: Then they yoked themselves to Baal of Peor and ate sacrifices offered to the dead;
verses.after: They bound themselves to Baal of Peor and ate sacrifices offered to the dead.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they yoked themselves to Baal of Peor and ate sacrifices offered to the dead;

verses.rationale: Preserves provocation and ensuing plague.
verses.before: they provoked the LORD to anger with their deeds, and a plague broke out among them.
verses.after: Their deeds provoked him, and a plague broke out among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: they provoked the LORD to anger with their deeds, and a plague broke out among them.

verses.rationale: Keeps decisive intervention without recasting the violent episode as prayer.
verses.before: Then Phinehas stood up and intervened, and the plague was stopped.
verses.after: Then Phinehas stood up and intervened, and the plague stopped.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Phinehas stood up and intervened, and the plague was stopped.

verses.rationale: Preserves reckoning language and enduring assessment.
verses.before: And that was counted to him as righteousness from generation to generation forever.
verses.after: This was counted to him as righteousness from generation to generation, forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: And that was counted to him as righteousness from generation to generation forever.

verses.rationale: Keeps the people's provocation and its cost to Moses.
verses.before: They angered him at the waters of Meribah, and it went ill with Moses on their account,
verses.after: They angered him at the waters of Meribah, and Moses suffered because of them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They angered him at the waters of Meribah, and it went ill with Moses on their account,

verses.rationale: Leaves whose spirit unresolved while identifying the rash speaker.
verses.before: for they made his spirit bitter, and he spoke rashly with his lips.
verses.after: They rebelled against his spirit, and Moses spoke rashly with his lips.
verses.tsw_comparator: for they made his spirit bitter, and he spoke rashly with his lips.

verses.rationale: Retains the destructive command without euphemism.
verses.before: They did not destroy the peoples, as the LORD commanded them,
verses.after: They did not destroy the peoples as the LORD had commanded them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They did not destroy the peoples, as the LORD commanded them,

verses.rationale: Preserves mixing and learned conduct as the narrated sequence.
verses.before: but mingled with the nations and learned to do as they did.
verses.after: Instead, they mingled with the nations and learned their practices.
verses.tsw_comparator: but mingled with the nations and learned to do as they did.

verses.rationale: Keeps service and snare image.
verses.before: They served their idols, which became a snare to them.
verses.after: They served their idols, which became a trap for them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They served their idols, which became a snare to them.

verses.rationale: Preserves both sexes of children and the named recipients.
verses.before: They sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons;
verses.after: They sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons.
verses.tsw_comparator: They sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons;

verses.rationale: Retains repeated blood, children, recipients, and land pollution.
verses.before: they poured out innocent blood, the blood of their sons and daughters, whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan, and the land was polluted with blood.
verses.after: They spilled innocent blood, the blood of their sons and daughters, whom they sacrificed to Canaan’s idols. The land was polluted with blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: they poured out innocent blood, the blood of their sons and daughters, whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan, and the land was polluted with blood.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sexual infidelity metaphor rather than generalizing misconduct.
verses.before: Thus they became unclean by their acts and played the harlot in their deeds.
verses.after: They defiled themselves by what they did and prostituted themselves through their practices.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus they became unclean by their acts and played the harlot in their deeds.

verses.rationale: Keeps the force of anger and revulsion toward his own people.
verses.before: Then the anger of the LORD was kindled against his people, and he abhorred his inheritance;
verses.after: The LORD’s anger burned against his people; he came to loathe his own inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the anger of the LORD was kindled against his people, and he abhorred his inheritance;

verses.rationale: Preserves divine handing-over and hostile rule.
verses.before: he gave them into the hand of the nations, so that people who hated them ruled over them.
verses.after: He handed them over to the nations, and those who hated them ruled over them.
verses.tsw_comparator: he gave them into the hand of the nations, so that those who hated them ruled over them.

verses.rationale: Keeps oppression and hand imagery.
verses.before: Their enemies oppressed them, and they were brought into subjection under their power.
verses.after: Their enemies oppressed them, and they were subdued under their hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their enemies oppressed them, and they were brought into subjection under their power.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated rescue, deliberate rebellion, and resulting abasement.
verses.before: Many times he delivered them, but they were rebellious in their purposes and were brought low through their iniquity.
verses.after: Time after time he rescued them, but they rebelled in their schemes and sank low through their guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Many times he delivered them, but they were rebellious in their purposes and were brought low through their iniquity.

verses.rationale: Keeps seeing and hearing as the turn toward compassion.
verses.before: Even so, he looked upon their distress, when he heard their cry.
verses.after: Yet he saw their distress when he heard their cry.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nevertheless, he looked upon their distress, when he heard their cry.

verses.rationale: Preserves covenant remembrance and relenting, with read-form abundance.
verses.before: For their sake he remembered his covenant, and relented according to the abundance of his steadfast love.
verses.after: He remembered his covenant for them and relented in his abundant faithful love.
verses.tsw_comparator: For their sake he remembered his covenant, and relented according to the abundance of his steadfast love.

verses.rationale: Keeps compassion mediated through captors.
verses.before: He caused them to be pitied by all people who held them captive.
verses.after: He made all their captors show them compassion.
verses.tsw_comparator: He caused them to be pitied by all those who held them captive.

verses.rationale: Retains gathering and the two purposes of deliverance.
verses.before: Save us, O LORD our God, and gather us from among the nations, that we may give thanks to your holy name and glory in your praise.
verses.after: Save us, LORD our God, and gather us from the nations, so we may thank your holy name and glory in praising you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Save us, O LORD our God, and gather us from among the nations, that we may give thanks to your holy name and glory in your praise.

verses.rationale: Preserves the book-closing blessing, communal response, and short name.
verses.before: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting! And let all the people say, “Amen!” Praise the LORD!
verses.after: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Let all the people say, “Amen!” Praise YAH!
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting! And let all the people say, “Amen!” Praise the LORD!

verses.rationale: Keeps the thanksgiving formula consistent with Psalm 106.
verses.before: Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good, for his steadfast love endures forever!
verses.after: Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good, for his steadfast love endures forever!

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated redemption and hand image.
verses.before: Let the redeemed of the LORD say so, whom he has redeemed from trouble
verses.after: Let those the LORD has redeemed say so, those he redeemed from the enemy’s hand,
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the redeemed of the LORD say so, whom he has redeemed from trouble

verses.rationale: Retains the source's sea rather than silently replacing it with south.
verses.before: and gathered in from the lands, from the east and from the west, from the north and from the south.
verses.after: those he gathered from the lands, from east and west, from north and the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: and gathered in from the lands, from the east and from the west, from the north and from the south.

verses.rationale: Makes the wandering group readable while preserving failed settlement.
verses.before: Some wandered in desert wastes, finding no way to a city to dwell in;
verses.after: Some wandered in desert wastelands; they found no road to a city where they could live.
verses.tsw_comparator: Some wandered in desert wastes, finding no way to a city to dwell in;

verses.rationale: Renders failing nephesh as exhausted life rather than disembodied soul.
verses.before: hungry and thirsty, their soul fainted within them.
verses.after: Hungry and thirsty, their lives were ebbing away.
verses.tsw_comparator: hungry and thirsty, their soul fainted within them.

verses.rationale: Retains the rescue verb distinct from later refrain variants.
verses.before: Then they cried to the LORD in their trouble, and he delivered them from their distress.
verses.after: Then they cried to the LORD in their distress, and he rescued them from their troubles.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they cried to the LORD in their trouble, and he delivered them from their distress.

verses.rationale: Preserves direction and the answer to the missing dwelling place.
verses.before: He led them by a straight way till they reached a city to dwell in.
verses.after: He led them along a straight road to a city where they could live.
verses.tsw_comparator: He led them by a straight way till they reached a city to dwell in.

verses.rationale: Establishes the repeated thanksgiving refrain without narrowing humanity.
verses.before: Let them give thanks to the LORD for his steadfast love, for his wondrous works to the children of humanity!
verses.after: Let them thank the LORD for his faithful love and his wonders for humanity.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them give thanks to the LORD for his steadfast love, for his wondrous works to the children of humanity!

verses.rationale: Keeps the bodily needs and their satisfaction.
verses.before: For he satisfies the longing soul, and the hungry soul he fills with good.
verses.after: For he satisfies the thirsty and fills the hungry with good things.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he satisfies the longing soul, and the hungry soul he fills with good.

verses.rationale: Retains darkness, death-shadow, and material confinement.
verses.before: Some sat in darkness and in the shadow of death, prisoners in affliction and in irons,
verses.after: Some sat in darkness and death’s shadow, prisoners bound in misery and iron,
verses.tsw_comparator: Some sat in darkness and in the shadow of death, prisoners in affliction and in irons,

verses.rationale: Keeps the two offenses and the divine title.
verses.before: for they had rebelled against the words of God and spurned the counsel of the Most High.
verses.after: because they had rebelled against God’s words and spurned the counsel of the Most High.
verses.tsw_comparator: for they had rebelled against the words of God and spurned the counsel of the Most High.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine agency, labor, and helpless stumbling.
verses.before: So he humbled their heart with hard labor; they fell down, with none to help.
verses.after: He humbled their hearts with hard labor; they stumbled, and no one helped.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he humbled their heart with hard labor; they fell down, with none to help.

verses.rationale: Retains saved as the source's variation on verse 6.
verses.before: Then they cried to the LORD in their trouble, and he saved them from their distress.
verses.after: Then they cried to the LORD in their distress, and he saved them from their troubles.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they cried to the LORD in their trouble, and he saved them from their distress.

verses.rationale: Keeps liberation tied to both repeated images.
verses.before: He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death, and burst their bonds apart.
verses.after: He brought them out of darkness and death’s shadow and broke their chains apart.
verses.tsw_comparator: He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death, and burst their bonds apart.

verses.rationale: Preserves the exact repeated thanksgiving refrain.
verses.before: Let them give thanks to the LORD for his steadfast love, for his wondrous works to the children of humanity!
verses.after: Let them thank the LORD for his faithful love and his wonders for humanity.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them give thanks to the LORD for his steadfast love, for his wondrous works to the children of humanity!

verses.rationale: Retains both metals and distinct breaking actions.
verses.before: For he shatters the doors of bronze and cuts in two the bars of iron.
verses.after: For he shattered bronze doors and cut through iron bars.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he shatters the doors of bronze and cuts in two the bars of iron.

verses.rationale: Preserves fools as the subject of suffering without adding a process of becoming foolish.
verses.before: Some were fools through their sinful ways, and because of their iniquities suffered affliction;
verses.after: Fools suffered for their rebellious ways, for their wrongs.
verses.tsw_comparator: Some were fools through their sinful ways, and because of their iniquities suffered affliction;

verses.rationale: Keeps aversion to all food and death's gate image.
verses.before: they loathed any kind of food, and they drew near to the gates of death.
verses.after: They could not bear any food and drew near the gates of death.
verses.tsw_comparator: they loathed any kind of food, and they drew near to the gates of death.

verses.rationale: Repeats the source wording of verse 13.
verses.before: Then they cried to the LORD in their trouble, and he saved them from their distress.
verses.after: Then they cried to the LORD in their distress, and he saved them from their troubles.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they cried to the LORD in their trouble, and he saved them from their distress.

verses.rationale: Preserves healing by the sent word and the pit/destruction expression.
verses.before: He sent out his word and healed them, and delivered them from their destruction.
verses.after: He sent his word and healed them; he delivered them from their pits of destruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: He sent out his word and healed them, and delivered them from their destruction.

verses.rationale: Maintains the refrain despite the source's scribal marking.
verses.before: Let them give thanks to the LORD for his steadfast love, for his wondrous works to the children of humanity!
verses.after: Let them thank the LORD for his faithful love and his wonders for humanity.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them give thanks to the LORD for his steadfast love, for his wondrous works to the children of humanity!

verses.rationale: Retains sacrificial worship and narrated deeds.
verses.before: And let them offer sacrifices of thanksgiving, and tell of his deeds in songs of joy!
verses.after: Let them offer sacrifices of thanksgiving and tell of his deeds with joyful shouts.
verses.tsw_comparator: And let them offer sacrifices of thanksgiving, and tell of his deeds in songs of joy!

verses.rationale: Preserves descent to sea and commercial purpose.
verses.before: Some went down to the sea in ships, doing business on the great waters;
verses.after: Some went down to the sea in ships, doing business on the mighty waters.
verses.tsw_comparator: Some went down to the sea in ships, doing business on the great waters;

verses.rationale: Keeps seafarers as witnesses and the deep as setting.
verses.before: they saw the deeds of the LORD, his wondrous works in the deep.
verses.after: They saw the LORD’s works, his wonders in the deep.
verses.tsw_comparator: they saw the deeds of the LORD, his wondrous works in the deep.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine speech and the wind-wave sequence.
verses.before: For he commanded and raised the stormy wind, which lifted up the waves of the sea.
verses.after: He spoke and raised a storm wind that lifted the sea’s waves.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he commanded and raised the stormy wind, which lifted up the waves of the sea.

verses.rationale: Keeps vertical extremes and the melting-life idiom.
verses.before: They mounted up to heaven; they went down to the depths; their courage melted away in their evil plight;
verses.after: They rose to the heavens and plunged into the depths; their courage melted in their misery.
verses.tsw_comparator: They mounted up to heaven; they went down to the depths; their courage melted away in their evil plight;

verses.rationale: Preserves intoxication comparison and swallowed wisdom image.
verses.before: they reeled and staggered like drunken men and were at their wits’ end.
verses.after: They reeled and staggered like drunks; all their skill was swallowed up.
verses.tsw_comparator: they reeled and staggered like drunken men and were at their wits’ end.

verses.rationale: Retains brought out as the fourth rescue refrain's distinct verb.
verses.before: Then they cried to the LORD in their trouble, and he delivered them from their distress.
verses.after: Then they cried to the LORD in their distress, and he brought them out of their troubles.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they cried to the LORD in their trouble, and he delivered them from their distress.

verses.rationale: Keeps the storm's hush and the waves' silence.
verses.before: He made the storm be still, and the waves of the sea were hushed.
verses.after: He stilled the storm to a whisper, and the waves fell silent.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made the storm be still, and the waves of the sea were hushed.

verses.rationale: Renders the rare destination term as harbor with desire intact.
verses.before: Then they were glad that the waters were quiet, and he brought them to their desired haven.
verses.after: They were glad when the waters grew calm, and he guided them to the harbor they longed for.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they were glad that the waters were quiet, and he brought them to their desired haven.

verses.rationale: Keeps the fourth thanksgiving refrain unchanged.
verses.before: Let them give thanks to the LORD for his steadfast love, for his wondrous works to the children of humanity!
verses.after: Let them thank the LORD for his faithful love and his wonders for humanity.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them give thanks to the LORD for his steadfast love, for his wondrous works to the children of humanity!

verses.rationale: Retains both public settings.
verses.before: Let them extol him in the congregation of the people, and praise him in the assembly of the elders.
verses.after: Let them exalt him in the people’s assembly and praise him in the council of elders.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them extol him in the congregation of the people, and praise him in the assembly of the elders.

verses.rationale: Preserves present-tense reversal and thirsty earth image.
verses.before: He turns rivers into a desert, springs of water into thirsty ground,
verses.after: He turns rivers into desert and springs of water into thirsty ground,
verses.tsw_comparator: He turns rivers into a desert, springs of water into thirsty ground,

verses.rationale: Keeps the stated moral cause and salination image.
verses.before: a fruitful land into a salty waste, because of the evil of its inhabitants.
verses.after: fruitful land into a salt waste, because of the evil of those who live there.
verses.tsw_comparator: a fruitful land into a salty waste, because of the evil of its inhabitants.

verses.rationale: Preserves the symmetrical reversal without merging water forms.
verses.before: He turns a desert into pools of water, a parched land into springs of water.
verses.after: He turns desert into pools of water and dry ground into flowing springs.
verses.tsw_comparator: He turns a desert into pools of water, a parched land into springs of water.

verses.rationale: Links settled hunger to the recurring dwelling-city image.
verses.before: And there he lets the hungry dwell, and they establish a city to live in;
verses.after: There he settles the hungry, and they build a city to live in.
verses.tsw_comparator: And there he lets the hungry dwell, and they establish a city to live in;

verses.rationale: Keeps the two agricultural activities and their yield.
verses.before: they sow fields and plant vineyards and get a fruitful yield.
verses.after: They sow fields and plant vineyards that yield a fruitful harvest.
verses.tsw_comparator: they sow fields and plant vineyards and get a fruitful yield.

verses.rationale: Preserves human increase and separate livestock protection.
verses.before: By his blessing they multiply greatly, and he does not let their livestock diminish.
verses.after: He blesses them, and they multiply greatly; he does not let their livestock dwindle.
verses.tsw_comparator: By his blessing they multiply greatly, and he does not let their livestock diminish.

verses.rationale: Keeps the unsettling reversal and all three causes.
verses.before: When they are diminished and brought low through oppression, evil, and sorrow,
verses.after: Then their numbers fall, and they are brought low through oppression, trouble, and sorrow.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they are diminished and brought low through oppression, evil, and sorrow,

verses.rationale: Retains humiliating judgment and pathless wandering.
verses.before: he pours contempt on princes and makes them wander in trackless wastes;
verses.after: He pours contempt on princes and makes them wander in a trackless waste.
verses.tsw_comparator: he pours contempt on princes and makes them wander in trackless wastes;

verses.rationale: Keeps social reversal and the flock comparison.
verses.before: but he raises up the needy out of affliction and makes their families like flocks.
verses.after: But he lifts the needy out of affliction and makes their families grow like flocks.
verses.tsw_comparator: but he raises up the needy out of affliction and makes their families like flocks.

verses.rationale: Preserves personified injustice and righteous response.
verses.before: The upright see it and are glad, and all wickedness shuts its mouth.
verses.after: The upright see it and rejoice; all injustice shuts its mouth.
verses.tsw_comparator: The upright see it and are glad, and all wickedness shuts its mouth.

verses.rationale: Keeps the wisdom invitation and plural manifestations of love.
verses.before: Whoever is wise, let him attend to these things; let them consider the steadfast love of the LORD.
verses.after: Whoever is wise will attend to these things and consider the LORD’s acts of faithful love.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever is wise, let him attend to these things; let them consider the steadfast love of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Binds separate title and first body record; preserves difficult glory expression.
verses.before: My heart is steadfast, O God. I will sing and make music; awake, my glory!
verses.after: A song. A psalm of David. My heart is steadfast, God. I will sing and make music with my glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: My heart is steadfast, O God. I will sing and make music; awake, my glory!

verses.rationale: Keeps personified instruments and dawn awakened by singer.
verses.before: Awake, harp and lyre! I will awaken the dawn.
verses.after: Wake up, harp and lyre! I will wake the dawn.
verses.tsw_comparator: Awake, harp and lyre! I will awaken the dawn.

verses.rationale: Retains public praise and two population terms.
verses.before: I will give thanks to you among the peoples, O LORD, and I will make music to you among the nations.
verses.after: I will thank you among the peoples, LORD; I will make music for you among the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will give thanks to you among the peoples, O LORD, and I will make music to you among the nations.

verses.rationale: Preserves beyond, differing from the related Psalm 57 line.
verses.before: For your steadfast love is great above the heavens, and your faithfulness reaches to the clouds.
verses.after: For your faithful love is great beyond the heavens; your faithfulness reaches the clouds.
verses.tsw_comparator: For your steadfast love is great above the heavens, and your faithfulness reaches to the clouds.

verses.rationale: Keeps paired heavenly and earthly scope.
verses.before: Be exalted above the heavens, O God, and let your glory be over all the earth.
verses.after: Be exalted above the heavens, God; let your glory be over all the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be exalted above the heavens, O God, and let your glory be over all the earth.

verses.rationale: Retains plural beloved, right hand, and singular answer me.
verses.before: So that your beloved may be delivered, save with your right hand and answer me.
verses.after: So that those you love may be rescued, save with your right hand and answer me.
verses.tsw_comparator: So that your beloved may be delivered, save with your right hand and answer me.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine speech, rejoicing, and territorial allocation.
verses.before: God has spoken in holiness: “I will exult; I will divide Shechem and measure out the Valley of Succoth.
verses.after: God has spoken in his holiness: “I will rejoice; I will divide Shechem and measure out the valley of Succoth.
verses.tsw_comparator: God has spoken in holiness: “I will exult; I will divide Shechem and measure out the Valley of Succoth.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated possession and two rule/defense images.
verses.before: Gilead is mine; Manasseh is mine; Ephraim is the helmet of my head; Judah is my scepter.
verses.after: Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine. Ephraim is the defense of my head; Judah is my ruler’s staff.
verses.tsw_comparator: Gilead is mine; Manasseh is mine; Ephraim is the helmet of my head; Judah is my scepter.

verses.rationale: Retains humiliating objects and divine first-person triumph.
verses.before: Moab is my washbasin; upon Edom I cast my sandal; over Philistia I shout in triumph.”
verses.after: Moab is my washbasin; over Edom I throw my sandal; over Philistia I shout in triumph.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moab is my washbasin; upon Edom I cast my sandal; over Philistia I shout in triumph.”

verses.rationale: Preserves paired questions and named destination.
verses.before: Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?
verses.after: Who will bring me into the fortified city? Who will guide me to Edom?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?

verses.rationale: Keeps communal complaint and repeated address.
verses.before: Have you not rejected us, O God? You do not go out, O God, with our armies.
verses.after: Have you not rejected us, God? You no longer go out with our armies, God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Have you not rejected us, O God? You do not go out, O God, with our armies.

verses.rationale: Preserves the contrast between requested aid and human rescue.
verses.before: Give us help against the foe, for human deliverance is worthless.
verses.after: Give us help against the foe; human deliverance is worthless.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give us help against the foe, for human deliverance is worthless.

verses.rationale: Keeps martial strength and divine trampling.
verses.before: With God we will do valiantly, and God will tread down our adversaries.
verses.after: With God we will act valiantly; he himself will trample our foes.
verses.tsw_comparator: With God we will do valiantly, and God will tread down our adversaries.

verses.rationale: Preserves inline title and urgent appeal against silence.
verses.before: O God of my praise, do not be silent.
verses.after: For the music director. Of David. A psalm. God of my praise, do not stay silent.
verses.tsw_comparator: O God of my praise, do not be silent.

verses.rationale: Retains mouth and tongue images with plural attackers.
verses.before: For wicked and deceitful mouths have opened against me; they speak to me with lying tongues.
verses.after: For wicked and deceitful mouths have opened against me; they speak to me with lying tongues.
verses.tsw_comparator: For wicked and deceitful mouths have opened against me; they speak to me with lying tongues.

verses.rationale: Preserves encirclement and undeserved hostility.
verses.before: They surround me with words of hatred and fight against me without cause.
verses.after: Words of hatred surround me; they attack me without cause.
verses.tsw_comparator: They surround me with words of hatred and fight against me without cause.

verses.rationale: Renders the compressed I-am-prayer idiom without losing the contrast.
verses.before: In return for my love they accuse me, but I am prayer.
verses.after: In return for my love they accuse me, but I give myself to prayer.
verses.tsw_comparator: In return for my love they accuse me, but I am prayer.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two inverted exchanges.
verses.before: They repay me evil for good and hatred for my love.
verses.after: They repay me with evil for good and hatred for my love.
verses.tsw_comparator: They repay me evil for good and hatred for my love.

verses.rationale: Preserves the abrupt singular target and legal accuser without supplying Satan.
verses.before: Appoint a wicked one over him, and let an accuser stand at his right hand.
verses.after: Appoint a wicked man over him; let an accuser stand at his right hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Appoint a wicked one over him, and let an accuser stand at his right hand.

verses.rationale: Keeps the judicial wish and troubling prayer-as-sin request.
verses.before: When he is judged, let him come out guilty, and let his prayer be counted as sin.
verses.after: When he is tried, let him come out guilty; let even his prayer be counted as sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he is judged, let him come out guilty, and let his prayer be counted as sin.

verses.rationale: Retains shortened life and transferred responsibility.
verses.before: Let his days be few; let another take his office.
verses.after: Let his days be few; let someone else take his office.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let his days be few; let another take his office.

verses.rationale: Keeps actual family harm and gendered relationships.
verses.before: Let his children be fatherless and his wife a widow.
verses.after: Let his children be fatherless and his wife a widow.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let his children be fatherless and his wife a widow.

verses.rationale: Retains intensified wandering and destitution; food supplies the implied sought need.
verses.before: Let his children wander and beg; let them seek food far from their ruins.
verses.after: Let his children wander and beg, searching for food far from their ruined homes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let his children wander and beg; let them seek food far from their ruins.

verses.rationale: Preserves total confiscation and loss of labor's fruit.
verses.before: Let a creditor seize all that he has, and let strangers plunder the fruit of his labor.
verses.after: Let a creditor seize everything he has; let strangers plunder what he worked for.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let a creditor seize all that he has, and let strangers plunder the fruit of his labor.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated refusal of mercy, including vulnerable children.
verses.before: Let there be no one to extend steadfast love to him, nor anyone to show favor to his fatherless children.
verses.after: Let no one extend faithful love to him; let no one show favor to his fatherless children.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let there be no one to extend steadfast love to him, nor anyone to show favor to his fatherless children.

verses.rationale: Preserves extinction and the specified generational horizon.
verses.before: Let his descendants be cut off; in the next generation let their name be blotted out.
verses.after: Let his descendants be cut off; let their name be wiped out in the next generation.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let his descendants be cut off; in the next generation let their name be blotted out.

verses.rationale: Keeps both parental lines and opposed remembrance/erasure.
verses.before: Let the iniquity of his ancestors be remembered before the LORD, and let the sin of his mother not be wiped away.
verses.after: Let the guilt of his fathers be remembered before the LORD; let his mother’s sin never be erased.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the iniquity of his ancestors be remembered before the LORD, and let the sin of his mother not be wiped away.

verses.rationale: Clarifies sins as the remembered object while preserving extinction of memory.
verses.before: Let them be before the LORD continually, so that God may cut off their memory from the earth.
verses.after: Let these sins always remain before the LORD, and let him cut off their memory from the earth,
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them be before the LORD continually, so that God may cut off their memory from the earth.

verses.rationale: Keeps the stated reason, victim's vulnerability, and lethal intent.
verses.before: For he did not remember to show steadfast love, but pursued the poor and needy and the brokenhearted, to put them to death.
verses.after: because he never thought to show faithful love. He pursued a poor and needy man, a brokenhearted man, to put him to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he did not remember to show steadfast love, but pursued the poor and needy and the brokenhearted, to put them to death.

verses.rationale: Retains the source's narrative reversal rather than making every clause a wish.
verses.before: He loved cursing; let it come upon him. He did not delight in blessing; let it remain far from him.
verses.after: He loved cursing, and it came upon him; he took no pleasure in blessing, and it stayed far from him.
verses.tsw_comparator: He loved cursing; let it come upon him. He did not delight in blessing; let it remain far from him.

verses.rationale: Preserves clothing and inward penetration images.
verses.before: He clothed himself with cursing like a garment; let it enter his body like water and his bones like oil.
verses.after: He wore cursing like a garment; it entered him like water, like oil into his bones.
verses.tsw_comparator: He clothed himself with cursing like a garment; let it enter his body like water and his bones like oil.

verses.rationale: Keeps the shift to a wish and both clothing objects.
verses.before: Let it be like a garment that wraps him, like a belt he always wears.
verses.after: Let it be the robe he wraps around himself, the belt he wears continually.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let it be like a garment that wraps him, like a belt he always wears.

verses.rationale: Retains reward/payment language and plural accusers' return.
verses.before: Let this be the reward from the LORD for my accusers, for people who speak evil against my life.
verses.after: Let this be the LORD’s payment to my accusers, to those who speak evil against my life.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let this be the reward from the LORD for my accusers, for those who speak evil against my life.

verses.rationale: Preserves both divine names and the grounds of appeal.
verses.before: But you, O LORD my Lord, act for me for your name’s sake. Because your steadfast love is good, deliver me.
verses.after: But you, LORD, my Lord, act for me for your name’s sake. Because your faithful love is good, rescue me.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you, O LORD my Lord, act for me for your name’s sake. Because your steadfast love is good, deliver me.

verses.rationale: Keeps social vulnerability and internal wound.
verses.before: For I am poor and needy, and my heart is wounded within me.
verses.after: For I am poor and needy, and my heart is wounded within me.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I am poor and needy, and my heart is wounded within me.

verses.rationale: Preserves two distinct frailty comparisons.
verses.before: I am passing away like a shadow when it lengthens; I am shaken off like a locust.
verses.after: I fade like a lengthening shadow; I am shaken off like a locust.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am passing away like a shadow when it lengthens; I am shaken off like a locust.

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily effects of fasting without spiritualizing them.
verses.before: My knees are weak from fasting; my flesh has grown lean, without fat.
verses.after: My knees give way from fasting; my body has wasted away, with no fat left.
verses.tsw_comparator: My knees are weak from fasting; my flesh has grown lean, without fat.

verses.rationale: Retains visible contempt and the head gesture.
verses.before: I have become an object of scorn to them; when they see me, they shake their heads.
verses.after: I have become an object of scorn to them; when they see me, they shake their heads.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have become an object of scorn to them; when they see me, they shake their heads.

verses.rationale: Keeps the paired pleas and covenant-love measure.
verses.before: Help me, O LORD my God; save me according to your steadfast love.
verses.after: Help me, LORD my God; save me in keeping with your faithful love.
verses.tsw_comparator: Help me, O LORD my God; save me according to your steadfast love.

verses.rationale: Preserves hand metaphor and emphatic divine agency.
verses.before: Let them know that this is your hand; you, O LORD, have done it.
verses.after: Let them know that this is your hand, that you, LORD, have done it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them know that this is your hand; you, O LORD, have done it.

verses.rationale: Keeps curse/blessing contrast and opponents/servant outcomes.
verses.before: Let them curse, but you will bless. When they rise up, let them be put to shame, but let your servant rejoice.
verses.after: They may curse, but you will bless. When they rise against me, let them be ashamed; let your servant rejoice.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them curse, but you will bless. When they rise up, let them be put to shame, but let your servant rejoice.

verses.rationale: Returns to the clothing image with both shame terms.
verses.before: Let my accusers be clothed with disgrace and wrap themselves in their shame as in a cloak.
verses.after: Let my accusers be clothed in disgrace; let them wrap themselves in shame as in a cloak.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let my accusers be clothed with disgrace and wrap themselves in their shame as in a cloak.

verses.rationale: Preserves bodily and public thanksgiving.
verses.before: With my mouth I will greatly thank the LORD; among many I will praise God.
verses.after: With my mouth I will greatly thank the LORD; in the midst of the crowd I will praise him.
verses.tsw_comparator: With my mouth I will greatly thank the LORD; in the midst of many I will praise God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the right-hand reversal of verse 6 and judicial threat to life.
verses.before: For the LORD stands at the right hand of the needy, to save that one from people who judge the life.
verses.after: For he stands at the right hand of the needy to save him from those who condemn him to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD stands at the right hand of the needy, to save that one from those who judge the life.

verses.rationale: Preserves title, distinct LORD/lord, and subjugation image without naming the addressee.
verses.before: The LORD says to my lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.”
verses.after: Of David. A psalm. The LORD’s declaration to my lord: “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD says to my lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the royal staff, Zion, and imperative to rule amid foes.
verses.before: The LORD sends out from Zion the scepter of your strength: “Rule among your enemies.”
verses.after: The LORD will extend your mighty staff from Zion: “Rule in the midst of your enemies.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD sends out from Zion the scepter of your strength: “Rule in the midst of your enemies.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the difficult youth/dew/dawn imagery without resolving all syntax.
verses.before: Your people offer themselves freely on the day of your power, in holy splendor. From the womb of the dawn, the dew of your youth is yours.
verses.after: Your people offer themselves freely on the day you muster your strength. In holy splendor, from the womb of dawn, the dew of your youth is yours.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your people offer themselves freely on the day of your power, in holy splendor. From the womb of the dawn, the dew of your youth is yours.

verses.rationale: Retains enduring priesthood and the difficult Melchizedek formula with a note.
verses.before: The LORD has sworn and will not change: “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.”
verses.after: The LORD has sworn and will not change his mind: “You are a priest forever, in the manner of Melchizedek.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has sworn and will not change: “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Adonai rather than inserting YHWH and retains crushed kings.
verses.before: The Lord is at your right hand; he shatters kings on the day of wrath.
verses.after: The Lord is at your right hand; he crushes kings on the day of his anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Lord is at your right hand; he shatters kings on the day of wrath.

verses.rationale: Keeps lethal judgment and the broad land image without sanitizing corpses.
verses.before: He judges among the nations, filling them with corpses; he shatters heads over the broad earth.
verses.after: He judges among the nations, leaving them full of corpses; he crushes heads across a vast land.
verses.tsw_comparator: He judges among the nations, filling them with corpses; he shatters heads over the broad earth.

verses.rationale: Retains unnamed subject and the unexplained therefore connection.
verses.before: He drinks from the torrent along the way; so he lifts up his head.
verses.after: He drinks from a stream beside the road; therefore he lifts his head.
verses.tsw_comparator: He drinks from the torrent along the way; therefore he lifts up his head.

verses.rationale: Keeps opening acclamation and two communal settings.
verses.before: Praise the LORD! I will give thanks to the LORD with my whole heart, in the council of the upright and in the congregation.
verses.after: Praise YAH! I will thank the LORD with my whole heart, in the company of the upright and in the assembly.
verses.tsw_comparator: Praise the LORD! I will give thanks to the LORD with my whole heart, in the council of the upright and in the congregation.

verses.rationale: Preserves attentive pursuit of works rather than passive admiration.
verses.before: Great are the works of the LORD, studied by everyone who delight in them.
verses.after: Great are the LORD’s works, studied by all who delight in them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Great are the works of the LORD, studied by all who delight in them.

verses.rationale: Retains paired glory terms and enduring righteousness.
verses.before: Splendor and majesty are God’s work, and God’s righteousness endures forever.
verses.after: His work is splendor and majesty; his righteousness stands forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Splendor and majesty are God’s work, and God’s righteousness endures forever.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine provision of remembrance and paired attributes.
verses.before: The LORD has made the wonders to be remembered; the LORD is gracious and compassionate.
verses.after: He has made his wonders remembered; the LORD is gracious and compassionate.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has made the wonders to be remembered; the LORD is gracious and compassionate.

verses.rationale: Retains food and covenant remembrance without an added condition.
verses.before: God gives food to people who fear the LORD; God remembers the covenant forever.
verses.after: He gives food to those who fear him; he remembers his covenant forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: God gives food to those who fear the LORD; God remembers the covenant forever.

verses.rationale: Preserves territorial gift as the displayed power.
verses.before: The LORD has shown the people the power of God’s works by giving them the inheritance of the nations.
verses.after: He has shown his people the power of his works by giving them the inheritance of nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has shown the people the power of God’s works by giving them the inheritance of the nations.

verses.rationale: Keeps hands, paired qualities, and precepts terminology.
verses.before: The works of God’s hands are truth and justice; all God’s precepts are trustworthy.
verses.after: The works of his hands are faithfulness and justice; all his precepts are trustworthy,
verses.tsw_comparator: The works of God’s hands are truth and justice; all God’s precepts are trustworthy.

verses.rationale: Carries preceding precepts into the enduring and ethical description.
verses.before: They are established forever and ever, performed in faithfulness and uprightness.
verses.after: firmly established forever and ever, enacted in faithfulness and uprightness.
verses.tsw_comparator: They are established forever and ever, performed in faithfulness and uprightness.

verses.rationale: Preserves three poetic units and reverent fear, not merely admiration.
verses.before: God sent redemption to the people and commanded the covenant forever. Holy and fearsome is God’s name.
verses.after: He sent redemption to his people; he ordained his covenant forever. Holy and fearsome is his name.
verses.tsw_comparator: God sent redemption to the people and commanded the covenant forever. Holy and fearsome is God’s name.

verses.rationale: Makes the implied practiced commands legible while preserving three final units.
verses.before: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom; good understanding belongs to everyone who practice it. God’s praise endures forever.
verses.after: Fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom. All who practice his precepts have good understanding. His praise stands forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom; good understanding belongs to all who practice it. God’s praise endures forever.

verses.rationale: Preserves singular exemplar and strong delight alongside fear.
verses.before: Praise the LORD! Happy is the one who fears the LORD, who greatly delights in God’s commandments.
verses.after: Praise YAH! Happy is the one who fears the LORD, who delights greatly in his commands.
verses.tsw_comparator: Praise the LORD! Happy is the one who fears the LORD, who greatly delights in God’s commandments.

verses.rationale: Keeps offspring and generation claims distinct.
verses.before: Their offspring will be mighty in the land; the generation of the upright will be blessed.
verses.after: His offspring will be mighty in the land; the generation of the upright will be blessed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their offspring will be mighty in the land; the generation of the upright will be blessed.

verses.rationale: Retains material wealth without turning the psalm into a formula.
verses.before: Wealth and riches are in their house, and their righteousness endures forever.
verses.after: Wealth and riches are in his house, and his righteousness stands forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wealth and riches are in their house, and their righteousness endures forever.

verses.rationale: Takes the virtues of the upright person while recording the possible divine reference.
verses.before: Light rises in the darkness for the upright— gracious, compassionate, and righteous.
verses.after: Light dawns in the darkness for the upright, for one who is gracious, compassionate, and righteous.
verses.tsw_comparator: Light rises in the darkness for the upright— gracious, compassionate, and righteous.

verses.rationale: Keeps lending, generosity, and just conduct together.
verses.before: It is well with the one who is gracious and lends, who conducts affairs with justice.
verses.after: It goes well for one who is generous and lends, who manages his affairs with justice.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is well with the one who is gracious and lends, who conducts affairs with justice.

verses.rationale: Preserves stability and lasting memory.
verses.before: For the righteous will never be shaken; they will be remembered forever.
verses.after: He will never be shaken; the righteous will be remembered forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the righteous will never be shaken; they will be remembered forever.

verses.rationale: Keeps feared report, steady heart, and trust.
verses.before: They are not afraid of bad news; their heart is firm, trusting in the LORD.
verses.after: He does not fear bad news; his heart is steadfast, trusting the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: They are not afraid of bad news; their heart is firm, trusting in the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains until and the conventional victorious look without adding destruction.
verses.before: Their heart is steady; they are not afraid, until they look in triumph on their foes.
verses.after: His heart is secure; he will not fear, until he looks in triumph on his foes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their heart is steady; they are not afraid, until they look in triumph on their foes.

verses.rationale: Preserves three units and the ancient horn image with vocabulary support.
verses.before: They have scattered abroad; they have given to the poor. Their righteousness endures forever; their horn is raised in honor.
verses.after: He gives freely to the needy; his righteousness stands forever; his horn is raised in honor.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have scattered abroad; they have given to the poor. Their righteousness endures forever; their horn is raised in honor.

verses.rationale: Keeps the bodily anger and vanishing desire in three units.
verses.before: The wicked see it and are angry; they gnash their teeth and melt away. The desire of the wicked will perish.
verses.after: The wicked see it and rage; they grind their teeth and waste away. The desire of the wicked comes to nothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wicked see it and are angry; they gnash their teeth and melt away. The desire of the wicked will perish.

verses.rationale: Retains all three praise calls and divine-name forms.
verses.before: Praise the LORD. Praise, O servants of the LORD; praise the name of the LORD.
verses.after: Praise YAH! Praise, you servants of the LORD; praise the name of the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Praise the LORD. Praise, O servants of the LORD; praise the name of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the present-to-endless temporal span.
verses.before: Blessed be the name of the LORD from this time forth and forevermore.
verses.after: Let the name of the LORD be blessed from now and forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed be the name of the LORD from this time forth and forevermore.

verses.rationale: Preserves the geographic and daily resonance of sunrise/sunset.
verses.before: From the rising of the sun to its setting, the name of the LORD is to be praised.
verses.after: From the rising of the sun to its setting, the name of the LORD is to be praised.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the rising of the sun to its setting, the name of the LORD is to be praised.

verses.rationale: Keeps two elevated scopes.
verses.before: The LORD is high above all nations, and his glory above the heavens.
verses.after: The LORD is high above all nations; his glory is above the heavens.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD is high above all nations, and his glory above the heavens.

verses.rationale: Retains the open question across the following verse.
verses.before: Who is like the LORD our God, who is seated on high,
verses.after: Who is like the LORD our God, enthroned on high,
verses.tsw_comparator: Who is like the LORD our God, who is seated on high,

verses.rationale: Keeps the surprising lowering needed even to see heaven.
verses.before: who looks far down on the heavens and the earth?
verses.after: who stoops to look on the heavens and the earth?
verses.tsw_comparator: who looks far down on the heavens and the earth?

verses.rationale: Preserves material degradation and upward movement.
