verses.tsw_comparator: Many are my persecutors and my adversaries, but I do not swerve from your testimonies.

verses.rationale: Retains strong revulsion rather than mild disappointment.
verses.before: I look at the faithless with disgust, because they do not keep your commands.
verses.after: I see the faithless and feel disgust, because they do not keep your utterance.
verses.tsw_comparator: I look at the faithless with disgust, because they do not keep your commands.

verses.rationale: Preserves seeing plea and love on both sides.
verses.before: Consider how I love your precepts! Give me life according to your steadfast love.
verses.after: See how I love your precepts; LORD, keep me alive according to your faithful love.
verses.tsw_comparator: Consider how I love your precepts! Give me life according to your steadfast love.

verses.rationale: Takes head as sum with beginning alternative noted.
verses.before: The sum of your word is truth, and every one of your righteous judgments endures forever.
verses.after: The sum of your word is truth; every one of your righteous judgments lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sum of your word is truth, and every one of your righteous judgments endures forever.

verses.rationale: Follows singular read form and contrasts human threat with divine awe.
verses.before: Princes persecute me without cause, but my heart stands in awe of your words.
verses.after: Rulers pursue me without cause, but my heart trembles at your word.
verses.tsw_comparator: Princes persecute me without cause, but my heart stands in awe of your words.

verses.rationale: Retains war-spoil comparison rather than generic treasure.
verses.before: I rejoice at your word like one who finds great spoil.
verses.after: I rejoice over your promise like someone who finds great plunder.
verses.tsw_comparator: I rejoice at your word like one who finds great spoil.

verses.rationale: Keeps doubled rejection opposite love.
verses.before: I hate and abhor falsehood, but I love your law.
verses.after: I hate and detest falsehood, but I love your instruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: I hate and abhor falsehood, but I love your law.

verses.rationale: Preserves the explicit number seven.
verses.before: Seven times a day I praise you for your righteous judgments.
verses.after: Seven times a day I praise you for your righteous judgments.
verses.tsw_comparator: Seven times a day I praise you for your righteous judgments.

verses.rationale: Keeps peace and obstacle-free walking claim.
verses.before: Great peace have people who love your law; nothing can make them stumble.
verses.after: Great peace belongs to those who love your instruction; nothing makes them stumble.
verses.tsw_comparator: Great peace have those who love your law; nothing can make them stumble.

verses.rationale: Retains hope joined to action.
verses.before: I hope for your salvation, O LORD, and I do your commandments.
verses.after: I hope for your salvation, LORD, and carry out your commands.
verses.tsw_comparator: I hope for your salvation, O LORD, and I do your commandments.

verses.rationale: Keeps personal commitment and intensified love.
verses.before: My soul keeps your testimonies; I love them exceedingly.
verses.after: I keep your testimonies with my whole being; I love them deeply.
verses.tsw_comparator: My soul keeps your testimonies; I love them exceedingly.

verses.rationale: Preserves two instruction terms and divine visibility.
verses.before: I keep your precepts and testimonies, for all my ways are before you.
verses.after: I keep your precepts and your testimonies, for all my ways lie before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I keep your precepts and testimonies, for all my ways are before you.

verses.rationale: Keeps approaching cry and word-grounded understanding.
verses.before: Let my cry come before you, O LORD; give me understanding according to your word!
verses.after: Let my cry come before you, LORD; give me understanding according to your word.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let my cry come before you, O LORD; give me understanding according to your word!

verses.rationale: Preserves parallel approach with rescue replacing understanding.
verses.before: Let my plea come before you; deliver me according to your promise.
verses.after: Let my plea come before you; rescue me according to your promise.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let my plea come before you; deliver me according to your promise.

verses.rationale: Keeps bubbling speech image and divine teaching.
verses.before: My lips will pour forth praise, for you teach me your statutes.
verses.after: Let praise pour from my lips, for you teach me your decrees.
verses.tsw_comparator: My lips will pour forth praise, for you teach me your statutes.

verses.rationale: Preserves tongue's response and all commands.
verses.before: My tongue will sing of your word, for all your commandments are right.
verses.after: Let my tongue sing of your utterance, for all your commands are righteous.
verses.tsw_comparator: My tongue will sing of your word, for all your commandments are right.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine hand and deliberate choice.
verses.before: Let your hand be ready to help me, for I have chosen your precepts.
verses.after: Let your hand be ready to help me, for I have chosen your precepts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let your hand be ready to help me, for I have chosen your precepts.

verses.rationale: Preserves longing and delight at the close.
verses.before: I long for your salvation, O LORD, and your law is my delight.
verses.after: I long for your salvation, LORD, and your instruction is my delight.
verses.tsw_comparator: I long for your salvation, O LORD, and your law is my delight.

verses.rationale: Keeps life for praise and judgments as aid.
verses.before: Let my soul live and praise you, and let your judgments help me.
verses.after: Let me live and praise you; let your judgments help me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let my soul live and praise you, and let your judgments help me.

verses.rationale: Preserves the unresolved lost-sheep ending beside remembered commands.
verses.before: I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek your servant, for I do not forget your commandments.
verses.after: I have wandered like a lost sheep. Seek your servant, for I have not forgotten your commands.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek your servant, for I do not forget your commandments.

verses.rationale: Preserves collection title and answered cry.
verses.before: In my distress I called to the LORD, and the LORD answered me.
verses.after: A song of ascents. In my distress I called to the LORD, and he answered me.
verses.tsw_comparator: In my distress I called to the LORD, and the LORD answered me.

verses.rationale: Keeps life at risk and two speech organs.
verses.before: O LORD, deliver my soul from lying lips, from a deceitful tongue.
verses.after: LORD, rescue my life from lying lips, from a deceitful tongue.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, deliver my soul from lying lips, from a deceitful tongue.

verses.rationale: Retains unanswered agent and direct address to tongue.
verses.before: What will be given to you, and what more will be done to you, you deceitful tongue?
verses.after: What will he give you, and what more will he add, deceitful tongue?
verses.tsw_comparator: What shall be given to you, and what more shall be done to you, you deceitful tongue?

verses.rationale: Preserves weapon and intense-fuel images as the answer.
verses.before: Sharp arrows of a warrior, with glowing coals of broom wood.
verses.after: A warrior’s sharpened arrows, with burning coals of broom wood!
verses.tsw_comparator: Sharp arrows of a warrior, with glowing coals of broom wood.

verses.rationale: Keeps both distant peoples rather than inventing one location.
verses.before: Woe to me, that I sojourn in Meshech, that I dwell among the tents of Kedar!
verses.after: Woe to me, living as a foreigner in Meshech, dwelling among the tents of Kedar!
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to me, that I sojourn in Meshech, that I dwell among the tents of Kedar!

verses.rationale: Retains weary duration and peace-haters.
verses.before: Too long has my soul dwelt with people who hate peace.
verses.after: Too long have I lived with those who hate peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: Too long has my soul dwelt with those who hate peace.

verses.rationale: Preserves compressed identity and hostile response.
verses.before: I am for peace; but when I speak, they are for war.
verses.after: I am for peace, but when I speak, they are for war.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am for peace; but when I speak, they are for war.

verses.rationale: Keeps the title's preposition and genuine question.
verses.before: I lift up my eyes to the hills— from where will my help come?
verses.after: A song for ascents. I lift my eyes toward the mountains. Where will my help come from?
verses.tsw_comparator: I lift up my eyes to the hills— from where will my help come?

verses.rationale: Retains creator identification as answer.
verses.before: My help comes from the LORD, who made heaven and earth.
verses.after: My help comes from the LORD, the maker of heaven and earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: My help comes from the LORD, who made heaven and earth.

verses.rationale: Preserves the wish form before verse 4's assurance.
verses.before: The LORD will not let your foot be moved; the one who keeps you will not slumber.
verses.after: May he not let your foot slip; may your guardian not doze.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will not let your foot be moved; the one who keeps you will not slumber.

verses.rationale: Keeps both sleep verbs and named community.
verses.before: Indeed, the one who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
verses.after: Look: Israel’s guardian neither dozes nor sleeps.
verses.tsw_comparator: Indeed, the one who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated name and shade beside the body.
verses.before: The LORD is your keeper; the LORD is your shade at your right hand.
verses.after: The LORD is your guardian; the LORD is your shade at your right hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD is your keeper; the LORD is your shade at your right hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves ancient paired hazards without rationalizing moonlight.
verses.before: The sun will not strike you by day, nor the moon by night.
verses.after: The sun will not strike you by day, nor the moon by night.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sun shall not strike you by day, nor the moon by night.

verses.rationale: Keeps guard repetition and comprehensive claim.
verses.before: The LORD will keep you from all harm; the LORD will keep your life.
verses.after: The LORD will guard you from all harm; he will guard your life.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will keep you from all harm; the LORD will keep your life.

verses.rationale: Preserves daily movement pair and temporal span.
verses.before: The LORD will keep your going out and your coming in from this time on and forevermore.
verses.after: The LORD will guard your going out and coming in, from now and forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will keep your going out and your coming in from this time on and forevermore.

verses.rationale: Keeps David title and quoted invitation.
verses.before: A Song of Ascents. Of David. I rejoiced when they said to me, "Let us go to the house of the LORD!"
verses.after: A song of ascents. Of David. I rejoiced when they said to me, “Let us go to the house of the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: A Song of Ascents. Of David. I rejoiced when they said to me, "Let us go to the house of the LORD!"

verses.rationale: Preserves communal arrival and address to city.
verses.before: Our feet are standing within your gates, O Jerusalem.
verses.after: Our feet are standing inside your gates, Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: Our feet are standing within your gates, O Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keeps compact construction image open to social resonance.
verses.before: Jerusalem, built as a city that is bound firmly together,
verses.after: Jerusalem, built as a city joined firmly together,
verses.tsw_comparator: Jerusalem, built as a city that is bound firmly together,

verses.rationale: Preserves both divine-name forms and testimony obligation.
verses.before: to which the tribes go up, the tribes of the LORD, a testimony for Israel, to give thanks to the name of the LORD.
verses.after: there the tribes go up, the tribes of YAH, as a testimony ordained for Israel, to thank the name of the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: to which the tribes go up, the tribes of the LORD, a testimony for Israel, to give thanks to the name of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps plural judicial seats and royal house.
verses.before: For there were set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.
verses.after: For there stand thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.
verses.tsw_comparator: For there were set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.

verses.rationale: Retains peace and security as related terms.
verses.before: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: "May people who love you be secure.
verses.after: Ask for Jerusalem’s peace: “May those who love you be secure.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: "May those who love you be secure.

verses.rationale: Preserves defensive and royal structures.
verses.before: May there be peace within your walls, security within your towers."
verses.after: May peace be within your ramparts, security within your palaces.”
verses.tsw_comparator: May there be peace within your walls, security within your towers."

verses.rationale: Keeps kin and companion categories and spoken blessing.
verses.before: For the sake of my family and friends, I will say, "Peace be within you."
verses.after: For the sake of my brothers and companions, I will say, “Peace be within you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For the sake of my family and friends, I will say, "Peace be within you."

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated for-the-sake and active pursuit.
verses.before: For the sake of the house of the LORD our God, I will seek your good.
verses.after: For the sake of the house of the LORD our God, I will seek your good.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the sake of the house of the LORD our God, I will seek your good.

verses.rationale: Keeps upward gaze and heavenly enthronement.
verses.before: To you I lift up my eyes, O you who are enthroned in the heavens.
verses.after: A song of ascents. To you I lift my eyes, you who are enthroned in the heavens.
verses.tsw_comparator: To you I lift up my eyes, O you who are enthroned in the heavens.

verses.rationale: Preserves enslaved relationships, both genders, and repeated hands.
verses.before: Look, as the eyes of servants look to the hand of their master, as the eyes of a female servant look to the hand of her mistress, so our eyes look to the LORD our God until God is gracious to us.
verses.after: As the eyes of slaves look to their masters’ hand, as a female slave looks to her mistress’s hand, so our eyes look to the LORD our God until he shows us favor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, as the eyes of servants look to the hand of their master, as the eyes of a female servant look to the hand of her mistress, so our eyes look to the LORD our God until God is gracious to us.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated plea and satiety image.
verses.before: Be gracious to us, O LORD, be gracious to us, for we have had more than enough contempt.
verses.after: Show us favor, LORD, show us favor, for we have had more than enough contempt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be gracious to us, O LORD, be gracious to us, for we have had more than enough contempt.

verses.rationale: Retains two oppressor descriptions and repeated excess.
verses.before: Our soul has had more than enough of the scorn of people who are at ease, of the contempt of the proud.
verses.after: We have had more than enough of the mockery of the complacent, the contempt of the proud.
verses.tsw_comparator: Our soul has had more than enough of the scorn of those who are at ease, of the contempt of the proud.

verses.rationale: Preserves interrupted communal prompt and unfinished condition.
verses.before: If it had not been the LORD who was on our side— let Israel now say—
verses.after: A song of ascents. Of David. If the LORD had not been for us— let Israel say it—
verses.tsw_comparator: If it had not been the LORD who was on our side— let Israel now say—

verses.rationale: Repeats condition before naming human attackers.
verses.before: if it had not been the LORD who was on our side when people rose up against us,
verses.after: if the LORD had not been for us when people rose against us,
verses.tsw_comparator: if it had not been the LORD who was on our side when people rose up against us,

verses.rationale: Keeps live swallowing and burning anger.
verses.before: then they would have swallowed us alive, when their anger was kindled against us;
verses.after: they would have swallowed us alive when their anger burned against us.
verses.tsw_comparator: then they would have swallowed us alive, when their anger was kindled against us;

verses.rationale: Preserves two flood descriptions and threatened life.
verses.before: then the waters would have swept us away, the torrent would have gone over us;
verses.after: The waters would have swept us away; the torrent would have passed over our lives.
verses.tsw_comparator: then the waters would have swept us away, the torrent would have gone over us;

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated passing-over and intensified waters.
verses.before: then over us would have gone the raging waters.
verses.after: The raging waters would have passed over our lives.
verses.tsw_comparator: then over us would have gone the raging waters.

verses.rationale: Retains predator image and withheld surrender.
verses.before: Blessed be the LORD, who has not given us as prey to their teeth!
verses.after: Blessed be the LORD, who did not give us as prey to their teeth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed be the LORD, who has not given us as prey to their teeth!

verses.rationale: Preserves bird comparison and repeated escape.
verses.before: We have escaped like a bird from the snare of the fowlers; the snare is broken, and we have escaped!
verses.after: We escaped like a bird from the hunters’ trap. The trap broke, and we escaped.
verses.tsw_comparator: We have escaped like a bird from the snare of the fowlers; the snare is broken, and we have escaped!

verses.rationale: Keeps communal help and creator formula.
verses.before: Our help is in the name of the LORD, who made heaven and earth.
verses.after: Our help is in the name of the LORD, the maker of heaven and earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Our help is in the name of the LORD, who made heaven and earth.

verses.rationale: Preserves mountain comparison and enduring stability.
verses.before: People who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion, which cannot be shaken but remains forever.
verses.after: A song of ascents. Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion, which cannot be shaken but stands forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion, which cannot be shaken but remains forever.

verses.rationale: Keeps geographic protection and repeated surrounding.
verses.before: As the mountains surround Jerusalem, so the LORD surrounds the people from now and forever.
verses.after: Mountains surround Jerusalem; so the LORD surrounds his people, from now and forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: As the mountains surround Jerusalem, so the LORD surrounds the people from now and forever.

verses.rationale: Preserves oppressive rule, allotment, and moral danger.
verses.before: For the scepter of wickedness will not rest upon the land allotted to the righteous, so that the righteous do not stretch out their hands toward injustice.
verses.after: The scepter of wickedness will not rest on the land allotted to the righteous, so that the righteous will not reach out their hands to do wrong.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the scepter of wickedness shall not rest upon the land allotted to the righteous, so that the righteous do not stretch out their hands toward injustice.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated good and inward uprightness.
verses.before: Do good, O LORD, to people who are good and to people who are upright in their hearts.
verses.after: Do good, LORD, to those who are good, to those whose hearts are upright.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do good, O LORD, to those who are good and to those who are upright in their hearts.

verses.rationale: Retains punitive wish before final peace blessing.
verses.before: But people who turn aside to their crooked ways— the LORD will lead them away with people who do evil. Peace be upon Israel!
verses.after: But those who turn onto crooked paths— may the LORD lead them away with evildoers. Peace be upon Israel!
verses.tsw_comparator: But those who turn aside to their crooked ways— the LORD will lead them away with those who do evil. Peace be upon Israel!

verses.rationale: Keeps past restoration and dream comparison.
verses.before: When the LORD restored the fortunes of Zion, we were like people who dream.
verses.after: A song of ascents. When the LORD restored Zion’s fortunes, we were like people dreaming.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the LORD restored the fortunes of Zion, we were like those who dream.

verses.rationale: Preserves doubled then and outsiders' recognition.
verses.before: Then our mouth was filled with laughter and our tongue with shouts of joy. Then they said among the nations, “The LORD has done great things for them.”
verses.after: Then our mouths filled with laughter and our tongues with joyful shouts. Then the nations said, “The LORD has done great things for them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then our mouth was filled with laughter and our tongue with shouts of joy. Then they said among the nations, “The LORD has done great things for them.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the shift from their report to our confession.
verses.before: The LORD has done great things for us; we are glad.
verses.after: The LORD has done great things for us, and we rejoiced.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has done great things for us; we are glad.

verses.rationale: Retains renewed petition beside past restoration and southern drylands.
verses.before: Restore our fortunes, O LORD, like streams in the Negeb.
verses.after: Restore our fortunes, LORD, like streams in the Negev.
verses.tsw_comparator: Restore our fortunes, O LORD, like streams in the Negeb.

verses.rationale: Keeps agricultural and emotional reversal.
verses.before: People who sow in tears will reap with shouts of joy.
verses.after: Those who sow in tears will reap with joyful shouts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who sow in tears will reap with shouts of joy.

verses.rationale: Preserves emphatic return and paired carrying images.
verses.before: The one who goes out weeping, carrying seed for sowing, will surely return with shouts of joy, carrying the sheaves.
verses.after: The one who goes out weeping, carrying seed to sow, will surely return with joyful shouts, carrying his sheaves.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who goes out weeping, carrying seed for sowing, will surely return with shouts of joy, carrying the sheaves.

verses.rationale: Preserves attribution and both repeated conditions.
verses.before: Unless the LORD builds the house, people who build it labor in vain. Unless the LORD guards the city, the watchman keeps awake in vain.
verses.after: A song of ascents. Of Solomon. Unless the LORD builds the house, its builders labor in vain. Unless the LORD guards the city, the guard keeps watch in vain.
verses.tsw_comparator: Unless the LORD builds the house, those who build it labor in vain. Unless the LORD guards the city, the watchman keeps awake in vain.

verses.rationale: Keeps anxious labor and sleep reading; while-asleep alternative noted.
verses.before: It is vain for you to rise early and sit up late, eating the bread of toil; for God gives sleep to the beloved.
verses.after: In vain you rise early and stay up late, eating the bread of painful toil; he gives sleep to the one he loves.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is vain for you to rise early and sit up late, eating the bread of toil; for God gives sleep to the beloved.

verses.rationale: Preserves male children in the warrior-household context.
verses.before: Look, children are a heritage from the LORD; the fruit of the womb is a reward.
verses.after: Look: sons are an inheritance from the LORD; the fruit of the womb is a reward.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, children are a heritage from the LORD; the fruit of the womb is a reward.

verses.rationale: Keeps military comparison and father's youth.
verses.before: Like arrows in the hand of a warrior are the children of one’s youth.
verses.after: Like arrows in a warrior’s hand are sons born in one’s youth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like arrows in the hand of a warrior are the children of one’s youth.

verses.rationale: Preserves man, plural they, and civic gate confrontation.
verses.before: Happy is the one whose quiver is filled with them. They will not be put to shame when they speak with enemies in the gate.
verses.after: Happy is the man whose quiver is full of them. They will not be ashamed when they speak with enemies at the gate.
verses.tsw_comparator: Happy is the one whose quiver is filled with them. They will not be put to shame when they speak with enemies in the gate.

verses.rationale: Keeps inclusive opening and way imagery.
verses.before: Blessed is everyone who fears the LORD, who walks in his ways!
verses.after: A song of ascents. Happy is everyone who fears the LORD, who walks in his ways.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed is everyone who fears the LORD, who walks in his ways!

verses.rationale: Preserves labor's enjoyed produce and double blessing.
verses.before: You will eat the fruit of the labor of your hands; you will be blessed, and it will be well with you.
verses.after: You will eat what your hands have worked for; you will be happy, and it will go well for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall eat the fruit of the labor of your hands; you shall be blessed, and it shall be well with you.

verses.rationale: Keeps gendered spouse and two agricultural family images.
verses.before: Your wife will be like a fruitful vine within your house; your children will be like olive shoots around your table.
verses.after: Your wife will be like a fruitful vine within your house; your children like olive shoots around your table.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your wife will be like a fruitful vine within your house; your children will be like olive shoots around your table.

verses.rationale: Preserves male household exemplar and fear.
verses.before: Look, thus will the man be blessed who fears the LORD.
verses.after: Look: this is how the man who fears the LORD is blessed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, thus shall the man be blessed who fears the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps source of blessing and lifelong civic good.
verses.before: The LORD bless you from Zion! May you see the prosperity of Jerusalem all the days of your life!
verses.after: May the LORD bless you from Zion; may you see Jerusalem prosper all your life.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD bless you from Zion! May you see the prosperity of Jerusalem all the days of your life!

verses.rationale: Retains generational wish and communal conclusion.
verses.before: May you see your children’s children! Peace be upon Israel!
verses.after: May you see your children’s children. Peace be upon Israel!
verses.tsw_comparator: May you see your children’s children! Peace be upon Israel!

verses.rationale: Preserves communal first-person memory and spoken prompt.
verses.before: “Greatly have they oppressed me from my youth”— let Israel now say—
verses.after: A song of ascents. “They have oppressed me greatly from my youth”— let Israel say it—
verses.tsw_comparator: “Greatly have they oppressed me from my youth”— let Israel now say—

verses.rationale: Keeps exact repeated suffering before resistance.
verses.before: “greatly have they oppressed me from my youth, yet they have not prevailed against me.
verses.after: “They have oppressed me greatly from my youth, but they have not overcome me.
verses.tsw_comparator: “greatly have they oppressed me from my youth, yet they have not prevailed against me.

verses.rationale: Follows singular read form furrow and retains bodily violence.
verses.before: Plowers plowed upon my back; they made their furrows long.
verses.after: Plowers plowed across my back; they made their furrow long.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Plowers plowed upon my back; they made their furrows long.

verses.rationale: Keeps righteousness shown through severed bonds.
verses.before: The LORD is righteous; God has cut the cords of the wicked.”
verses.after: The LORD is righteous; he has cut the cords of the wicked.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD is righteous; God has cut the cords of the wicked.”

verses.rationale: Preserves wish against a specified group.
verses.before: Let everyone who hate Zion be put to shame and turned backward.
verses.after: May all who hate Zion be ashamed and driven back.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let all who hate Zion be put to shame and turned backward.

verses.rationale: Keeps thin-soil image and uncertain pulling verb with note.
verses.before: Let them be like grass on the housetops, which withers before it is pulled up,
verses.after: May they be like grass on rooftops, which dries up before it can be pulled,
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them be like grass on the housetops, which withers before it is pulled up,

verses.rationale: Retains the two empty harvest gestures.
verses.before: with which the reaper does not fill the hand, nor the binder of sheaves the arms,
verses.after: which never fills the reaper’s hand or the sheaf-binder’s arms.
verses.tsw_comparator: with which the reaper does not fill the hand, nor the binder of sheaves the arms,

verses.rationale: Preserves withheld harvest blessing and both divine names.
verses.before: and people who pass by do not say, “The blessing of the LORD be upon you; we bless you in the name of the LORD.”
verses.after: May passersby never say, “The LORD’s blessing be upon you; we bless you in the name of the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and those who pass by do not say, “The blessing of the LORD be upon you; we bless you in the name of the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Keeps depth image without inventing its cause.
verses.before: Out of the depths I cry to you, O LORD.
verses.after: A song of ascents. From the depths I call to you, LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Out of the depths I cry to you, O LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves Adonai and listening anatomy.
verses.before: Lord, hear my voice! Let your ears be attentive to the sound of my pleas for mercy.
verses.after: Lord, hear my voice; let your ears attend to my pleas for mercy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Lord, hear my voice! Let your ears be attentive to the sound of my pleas for mercy.

verses.rationale: Keeps both divine titles and judicial standing question.
verses.before: If you, O LORD, should mark iniquities, Lord, who could stand?
verses.after: If you kept account of wrongs, YAH, Lord, who could stand?
verses.tsw_comparator: If you, O LORD, should mark iniquities, Lord, who could stand?

verses.rationale: Retains surprising forgiveness-to-fear purpose.
verses.before: But with you there is forgiveness, so that you may be held in awe.
verses.after: But forgiveness is with you, so that you may be feared.
verses.tsw_comparator: But with you there is forgiveness, so that you may be held in awe.

verses.rationale: Keeps intensified waiting and hope.
verses.before: I wait for the LORD; my whole being waits, and in the LORD’s word I hope.
verses.after: I wait for the LORD; my whole being waits, and I hope in his word.
verses.tsw_comparator: I wait for the LORD; my whole being waits, and in the LORD’s word I hope.

verses.rationale: Preserves deliberate repeated comparison.
verses.before: My whole being waits for the Lord more than people who watch for the morning, more than people who watch for the morning.
verses.after: My whole being waits for the Lord more than watchmen for morning, more than watchmen for morning.
verses.tsw_comparator: My whole being waits for the Lord more than those who watch for the morning, more than those who watch for the morning.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated divine name and with-him structure.
verses.before: O Israel, hope in the LORD! For with the LORD there is steadfast love, and with the LORD is plentiful redemption.
verses.after: Israel, hope in the LORD, for with the LORD is faithful love, and with him is abundant redemption.
verses.tsw_comparator: O Israel, hope in the LORD! For with the LORD there is steadfast love, and with the LORD is plentiful redemption.

verses.rationale: Preserves emphatic agent and comprehensive redemption.
verses.before: The LORD will redeem Israel from all its iniquities.
verses.after: He himself will redeem Israel from all its wrongs.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will redeem Israel from all its iniquities.

verses.rationale: Keeps heart/eyes and restraint about inaccessible matters.
verses.before: O LORD, my heart is not proud, and my eyes are not raised too high. I do not occupy myself with things too great or too wondrous for me.
verses.after: A song of ascents. Of David. LORD, my heart is not proud and my eyes are not haughty. I do not occupy myself with things too great or with wonders beyond me.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, my heart is not proud, and my eyes are not raised too high. I do not occupy myself with things too great or too wondrous for me.

verses.rationale: Retains weaned child and unusual inward self-comparison.
verses.before: Surely I have calmed and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with its mother; like a weaned child is my soul within me.
verses.after: Surely I have calmed and quieted my soul, like a weaned child against its mother; like a weaned child, my soul rests against me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Surely I have calmed and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with its mother; like a weaned child is my soul within me.

verses.rationale: Keeps communal invitation following personal quiet.
verses.before: O Israel, hope in the LORD from now and forever.
verses.after: Israel, hope in the LORD from now and forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: O Israel, hope in the LORD from now and forever.

verses.rationale: Preserves memory plea and affliction rather than assumed humility.
verses.before: O LORD, remember David and all his affliction,
verses.after: A song of ascents. LORD, remember David and all the hardship he endured,
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, remember David and all his affliction,

verses.rationale: Keeps oath, vow, and ancestral divine title.
verses.before: how he swore to the LORD and vowed to the Mighty One of Jacob:
verses.after: how he swore to the LORD and vowed to the Mighty One of Jacob:
verses.tsw_comparator: how he swore to the LORD and vowed to the Mighty One of Jacob:

verses.rationale: Renders oath's conditional negatives as firm refusal.
verses.before: “I will not enter the tent of my house or go up onto the couch of my bed;
verses.after: “I will not enter my house or climb into my bed;
verses.tsw_comparator: “I will not enter the tent of my house or go up onto the couch of my bed;

verses.rationale: Keeps paired bodily sleep images.
verses.before: I will not give sleep to my eyes or slumber to my eyelids
verses.after: I will not give sleep to my eyes or slumber to my eyelids,
verses.tsw_comparator: I will not give sleep to my eyes or slumber to my eyelids

verses.rationale: Preserves endpoint and repeated ancestral title.
verses.before: until I find a place for the LORD, a dwelling place for the Mighty One of Jacob.”
verses.after: until I find a place for the LORD, a dwelling for the Mighty One of Jacob.”
verses.tsw_comparator: until I find a place for the LORD, a dwelling place for the Mighty One of Jacob.”

verses.rationale: Retains ambiguous it and both place names.
verses.before: Look, we heard of it in Ephrathah; we found it in the fields of Jaar.
verses.after: We heard of it in Ephrathah; we found it in the fields of Jaar.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, we heard of it in Ephrathah; we found it in the fields of Jaar.

verses.rationale: Keeps communal movement and throne imagery.
verses.before: “Let us go to God’s dwelling place; let us bow down at God’s footstool.”
verses.after: Let us enter his dwelling; let us bow down at his footstool.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Let us go to God’s dwelling place; let us bow down at God’s footstool.”

verses.rationale: Preserves divine movement with the ark.
verses.before: Rise, O LORD, to your resting place, you and the ark of your strength.
verses.after: Rise, LORD, to your resting place, you and the ark of your strength.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rise, O LORD, to your resting place, you and the ark of your strength.

verses.rationale: Keeps clothing metaphor and worshipers' response.
verses.before: Let your priests be clothed with righteousness, and let your faithful ones shout for joy.
verses.after: Let your priests be clothed with righteousness; let your faithful ones shout for joy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let your priests be clothed with righteousness, and let your faithful ones shout for joy.

verses.rationale: Preserves face-turning rejection image and unnamed anointed king.
verses.before: For the sake of David your servant, do not turn away the face of your anointed.
verses.after: For the sake of David your servant, do not turn away the face of your anointed one.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the sake of David your servant, do not turn away the face of your anointed.

verses.rationale: Keeps binding oath and bodily descent without naming successor.
verses.before: The LORD swore to David in truth and will not turn from it: “One of the fruit of your body I will set upon your throne.
verses.after: The LORD swore a true oath to David and will not turn back from it: “I will set one of your own offspring on your throne.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD swore to David in truth and will not turn from it: “One of the fruit of your body I will set upon your throne.

verses.rationale: Preserves explicit condition and multigenerational promise.
verses.before: If your children keep my covenant and my testimony that I teach them, their children also, forever, will sit upon your throne.”
verses.after: If your sons keep my covenant and the testimonies I teach them, their sons too will sit on your throne forever.”
verses.tsw_comparator: If your children keep my covenant and my testimony that I teach them, their children also, forever, shall sit upon your throne.”

verses.rationale: Keeps choice and desire introducing divine speech.
verses.before: For the LORD has chosen Zion; God has desired it as a dwelling place:
verses.after: For the LORD has chosen Zion; he has desired it as his dwelling:
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD has chosen Zion; God has desired it as a dwelling place:

verses.rationale: Retains first-person declaration and repeated desire.
verses.before: “This is my resting place forever; here I will dwell, for I have desired it.
verses.after: “This is my resting place forever; here I will dwell, for I have desired it.
verses.tsw_comparator: “This is my resting place forever; here I will dwell, for I have desired it.

verses.rationale: Keeps intensified blessing and material food for poor.
verses.before: I will abundantly bless her provisions; I will satisfy her poor with bread.
verses.after: I will richly bless its provisions; I will satisfy its needy people with bread.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will abundantly bless her provisions; I will satisfy her poor with bread.

verses.rationale: Preserves changed clothing term from verse 9 and intensified joy.
verses.before: Her priests I will clothe with salvation, and her faithful ones will shout aloud for joy.
verses.after: I will clothe its priests with salvation, and its faithful ones will shout aloud for joy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Her priests I will clothe with salvation, and her faithful ones will shout aloud for joy.

verses.rationale: Keeps both dynastic images without flattening them into power.
verses.before: There I will cause a horn to sprout for David; I have prepared a lamp for my anointed.
verses.after: There I will make a horn sprout for David; I have prepared a lamp for my anointed one.
verses.tsw_comparator: There I will cause a horn to sprout for David; I have prepared a lamp for my anointed.

verses.rationale: Preserves clothing reversal and growing crown image.
verses.before: His enemies I will clothe with shame, but upon him his crown will flourish.”
verses.after: I will clothe his enemies with shame, but his crown will blossom upon him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: His enemies I will clothe with shame, but upon him his crown will flourish.”

verses.rationale: Keeps kinship and shared dwelling without adding an abstract unity noun.
verses.before: Look, how good and how pleasant it is when brothers dwell together in unity!
verses.after: A song of ascents. Of David. Look how good and pleasant it is when brothers dwell together!
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is when brothers dwell together in unity!

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated downward flow and named priest.
verses.before: It is like the precious oil on the head, running down on the beard, on the beard of Aaron, running down on the collar of his robes!
verses.after: It is like fine oil on the head, running down the beard, Aaron’s beard, running down to the collar of his robes.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is like the precious oil on the head, running down on the beard, on the beard of Aaron, running down on the collar of his robes!

verses.rationale: Keeps poetic geography, repeated descent, and life blessing.
verses.before: It is like the dew of Hermon, which falls on the mountains of Zion! For there the LORD has commanded the blessing, life forevermore.
verses.after: It is like the dew of Hermon running down on the mountains of Zion. For there the LORD commanded the blessing: life forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is like the dew of Hermon, which falls on the mountains of Zion! For there the LORD has commanded the blessing, life forevermore.

verses.rationale: Preserves three LORD occurrences and night service.
verses.before: Look, bless the LORD, all you servants of the LORD who stand in the house of the LORD by night.
verses.after: A song of ascents. Come, bless the LORD, all you servants of the LORD who stand in the house of the LORD through the nights.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, bless the LORD, all you servants of the LORD who stand in the house of the LORD by night.

verses.rationale: Takes holy place direction while noting holiness alternative.
verses.before: Lift up your hands toward the holy place and bless the LORD.
verses.after: Lift your hands toward the sanctuary and bless the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Lift up your hands toward the holy place and bless the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps singular recipient and creator's blessing.
verses.before: May the LORD bless you from Zion, the maker of heaven and earth.
verses.after: May the LORD, the maker of heaven and earth, bless you from Zion.
verses.tsw_comparator: May the LORD bless you from Zion, the maker of heaven and earth.

verses.rationale: Keeps three calls and both divine-name forms.
verses.before: Praise the LORD! Praise the name of the LORD; give praise, servants of the LORD,
verses.after: Praise YAH! Praise the name of the LORD; praise him, servants of the LORD,
verses.tsw_comparator: Praise the LORD! Praise the name of the LORD; give praise, servants of the LORD,

verses.rationale: Preserves worshipers' location and communal our.
verses.before: you who stand in the house of the LORD, in the courts of the house of our God.
verses.after: you who stand in the house of the LORD, in the courts of the house of our God.
verses.tsw_comparator: you who stand in the house of the LORD, in the courts of the house of our God.

verses.rationale: Keeps short name and pleasant praise/name ambiguity.
verses.before: Praise the LORD, for the LORD is good; make music to God’s name, for it is pleasant.
verses.after: Praise YAH, for the LORD is good; make music for his name, for it is pleasant.
verses.tsw_comparator: Praise the LORD, for the LORD is good; make music to God’s name, for it is pleasant.

verses.rationale: Preserves choice, parallel names, and possession term.
verses.before: For the LORD has chosen Jacob for himself, Israel as God’s treasured possession.
verses.after: For YAH has chosen Jacob for himself, Israel as his treasured possession.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD has chosen Jacob for himself, Israel as God’s treasured possession.

verses.rationale: Keeps personal knowledge and explicit comparison with gods.
verses.before: For I know that the LORD is great, and our Lord is above all gods.
verses.after: I know that the LORD is great, that our Lord is above all gods.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I know that the LORD is great, and our Lord is above all gods.

verses.rationale: Preserves all four cosmic domains.
verses.before: Whatever the LORD pleases, God does, in the heavens and on the earth, in the seas and all the depths.
verses.after: Whatever the LORD pleases, he does, in heaven and on earth, in the seas and all the depths.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whatever the LORD pleases, God does, in the heavens and on the earth, in the seas and all the depths.

verses.rationale: Keeps weather sequence and ancient storehouse image.
verses.before: God raises clouds from the ends of the earth, makes lightning for the rain, and brings out the wind from storehouses.
verses.after: He raises clouds from the ends of the earth; he makes lightning for the rain and brings wind out of his storehouses.
verses.tsw_comparator: God raises clouds from the ends of the earth, makes lightning for the rain, and brings out the wind from storehouses.

verses.rationale: Preserves death and both victim categories.
verses.before: God struck the firstborn of Egypt, from human being to animal.
verses.after: He struck down Egypt’s firstborn, both human and animal.
verses.tsw_comparator: God struck the firstborn of Egypt, from human being to animal.

verses.rationale: Keeps direct address to Egypt and named targets.
verses.before: God sent signs and wonders into your midst, O Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his servants.
verses.after: He sent signs and wonders into your midst, Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his servants.
verses.tsw_comparator: God sent signs and wonders into your midst, O Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his servants.

verses.rationale: Preserves explicit killing and introduction to list.
verses.before: God struck many nations and killed mighty kings:
verses.after: He struck many nations and killed mighty kings:
verses.tsw_comparator: God struck many nations and killed mighty kings:

verses.rationale: Keeps names, titles, and comprehensive kingdoms.
verses.before: Sihon king of the Amorites, Og king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan.
verses.after: Sihon king of the Amorites, Og king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sihon king of the Amorites, Og king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated inheritance and recipient.
verses.before: God gave their land as a heritage, a heritage to Israel, God’s people.
verses.after: He gave their land as an inheritance, an inheritance to Israel his people.
verses.tsw_comparator: God gave their land as a heritage, a heritage to Israel, God’s people.

verses.rationale: Keeps both addresses and name/remembrance parallel.
verses.before: O LORD, your name is forever; O LORD, your remembrance is from generation to generation.
verses.after: LORD, your name lasts forever; LORD, your remembrance lasts through every generation.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, your name is forever; O LORD, your remembrance is from generation to generation.

verses.rationale: Renders judgment as vindication while retaining relenting.
verses.before: For the LORD will vindicate the people and have compassion on the servants.
verses.after: For the LORD will vindicate his people and relent toward his servants.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD will vindicate the people and have compassion on the servants.

verses.rationale: Keeps materials and human manufacture consistent with Psalm 115.
verses.before: The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of human hands.
verses.after: The nations’ idols are silver and gold, the work of human hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of human hands.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated idol critique.
verses.before: They have mouths but do not speak; they have eyes but do not see.
verses.after: They have mouths but cannot speak; they have eyes but cannot see.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have mouths but do not speak; they have eyes but do not see.

verses.rationale: Keeps this psalm's breath clause rather than importing Psalm 115's nose.
verses.before: They have ears but do not hear; there is no breath in their mouths.
verses.after: They have ears but cannot listen; there is not even breath in their mouths.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have ears but do not hear; there is no breath in their mouths.

verses.rationale: Preserves the shared warning of resemblance.
verses.before: People who make them become like them, as do everyone who trust in them.
verses.after: Those who make them become like them, as does everyone who trusts in them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who make them become like them, as do all who trust in them.

verses.rationale: Keeps two named groups and repeated blessing.
verses.before: House of Israel, bless the LORD! House of Aaron, bless the LORD!
verses.after: House of Israel, bless the LORD! House of Aaron, bless the LORD!
verses.tsw_comparator: House of Israel, bless the LORD! House of Aaron, bless the LORD!

verses.rationale: Preserves added Levitical house and three name occurrences.
verses.before: House of Levi, bless the LORD! You who fear the LORD, bless the LORD!
verses.after: House of Levi, bless the LORD! You who fear the LORD, bless the LORD!
verses.tsw_comparator: House of Levi, bless the LORD! You who fear the LORD, bless the LORD!

verses.rationale: Keeps Zion/Jerusalem and final short-name praise.
verses.before: Blessed be the LORD from Zion, the One who dwells in Jerusalem. Praise the LORD!
verses.after: Blessed from Zion be the LORD, who dwells in Jerusalem. Praise YAH!
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed be the LORD from Zion, the One who dwells in Jerusalem. Praise the LORD!

verses.rationale: Establishes the refrain that remains in every verse.
verses.before: Give thanks to the LORD, for God is good, for God’s steadfast love endures forever.
verses.after: Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give thanks to the LORD, for God is good, for God’s steadfast love endures forever.

verses.rationale: Preserves superlative title and full refrain.
verses.before: Give thanks to the God of gods, for God’s steadfast love endures forever.
verses.after: Give thanks to the God of gods; his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give thanks to the God of gods, for God’s steadfast love endures forever.

verses.rationale: Keeps lord title distinct from YHWH.
verses.before: Give thanks to the Lord of lords, for God’s steadfast love endures forever.
verses.after: Give thanks to the Lord of lords; his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give thanks to the Lord of lords, for God’s steadfast love endures forever.

verses.rationale: Carries thanksgiving syntax into sole wonder-worker.
verses.before: To the One who alone does great wonders, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;
verses.after: To him who alone does great wonders— his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: To the One who alone does great wonders, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;

verses.rationale: Preserves creation by understanding and refrain.
verses.before: to the One who made the heavens with understanding, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;
verses.after: who made the heavens with understanding— his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: to the One who made the heavens with understanding, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;

verses.rationale: Keeps ancient earth-over-waters image.
verses.before: to the One who spread out the earth over the waters, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;
verses.after: who spread the earth over the waters— his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: to the One who spread out the earth over the waters, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;

verses.rationale: Preserves plural lights introducing next two verses.
verses.before: to the One who made the great lights, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;
verses.after: who made the great lights— his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: to the One who made the great lights, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;

verses.rationale: Keeps daytime dominion and refrain.
verses.before: the sun to rule the day, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;
verses.after: the sun to rule by day— his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: the sun to rule the day, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;

verses.rationale: Retains both nocturnal lights and rule.
verses.before: the moon and stars to rule the night, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;
verses.after: the moon and stars to rule by night— his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: the moon and stars to rule the night, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;

verses.rationale: Keeps the lethal historical act alongside the unchanged refrain.
verses.before: To the One who struck Egypt through their firstborn, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;
verses.after: To him who struck Egypt through its firstborn— his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: To the One who struck Egypt through their firstborn, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;

verses.rationale: Preserves exodus movement and population distinction.
verses.before: and brought Israel out from among them, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;
verses.after: and brought Israel out from among them— his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: and brought Israel out from among them, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;

verses.rationale: Keeps paired bodily power images.
verses.before: with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;
verses.after: with a strong hand and an outstretched arm— his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;

verses.rationale: Preserves cutting imagery and Hebrew sea designation.
verses.before: to the One who divided the Sea of Reeds into parts, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;
verses.after: To him who cut the Sea of Reeds into parts— his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: to the One who divided the Sea of Reeds into parts, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;

verses.rationale: Keeps passage through the sea, not around it.
verses.before: and made Israel pass through the midst of it, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;
verses.after: and brought Israel through its midst— his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: and made Israel pass through the midst of it, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;

verses.rationale: Preserves shaking verb and destructive contrast.
verses.before: but shook off Pharaoh and his army into the Sea of Reeds, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;
verses.after: but shook Pharaoh and his army into the Sea of Reeds— his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: but shook off Pharaoh and his army into the Sea of Reeds, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;

verses.rationale: Keeps wilderness guidance and full refrain.
verses.before: to the One who led the people through the wilderness, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;
verses.after: To him who led his people through the wilderness— his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: to the One who led the people through the wilderness, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;

verses.rationale: Preserves royal victims and striking verb.
verses.before: To the One who struck great kings, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;
verses.after: who struck down great kings— his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: To the One who struck great kings, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;

verses.rationale: Keeps explicit killing distinct from verse 17.
verses.before: and killed mighty kings, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;
verses.after: and killed mighty kings— his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: and killed mighty kings, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;

verses.rationale: Preserves the first king and people.
verses.before: Sihon, king of the Amorites, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;
verses.after: Sihon king of the Amorites— his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sihon, king of the Amorites, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;

verses.rationale: Preserves the second king and territory.
verses.before: and Og, king of Bashan, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;
verses.after: and Og king of Bashan— his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Og, king of Bashan, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;

verses.rationale: Keeps dispossession and inherited territory.
verses.before: and gave their land as a heritage, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;
verses.after: and gave their land as an inheritance— his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: and gave their land as a heritage, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated inheritance and servant designation.
verses.before: a heritage to Israel, God’s servant, for God’s steadfast love endures forever.
verses.after: an inheritance to Israel his servant— his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: a heritage to Israel, God’s servant, for God’s steadfast love endures forever.

verses.rationale: Keeps shift to first-person communal memory.
verses.before: God remembered us in our low estate, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;
verses.after: He remembered us when we were brought low; his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: God remembered us in our low estate, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;

verses.rationale: Retains force of liberating verb.
verses.before: and rescued us from our foes, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;
verses.after: he tore us free from our foes; his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: and rescued us from our foes, for God’s steadfast love endures forever;

verses.rationale: Preserves all flesh, including nonhuman creatures.
verses.before: the One who gives food to all flesh, for God’s steadfast love endures forever.
verses.after: He gives food to all flesh; his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: the One who gives food to all flesh, for God’s steadfast love endures forever.

verses.rationale: Keeps closing invitation and final complete refrain.
verses.before: Give thanks to the God of heaven, for God’s steadfast love endures forever.
verses.after: Give thanks to the God of heaven; his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give thanks to the God of heaven, for God’s steadfast love endures forever.

verses.rationale: Preserves exile setting and memory-triggered grief.
verses.before: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down and wept when we remembered Zion.
verses.after: By Babylon’s rivers we sat down and wept when we remembered Zion.
verses.tsw_comparator: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down and wept when we remembered Zion.

verses.rationale: Keeps hanging instruments and tree identification with alternative noted.
verses.before: On the willows there we hung up our lyres.
verses.after: On the poplars there we hung our lyres.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the willows there we hung up our lyres.

verses.rationale: Preserves coercive demand rather than voluntary performance.
verses.before: For there our captors asked us for songs, and our tormentors asked for mirth: “Sing for us one of the songs of Zion!”
verses.after: For there our captors demanded songs, our tormentors demanded joy: “Sing us one of Zion’s songs!”
verses.tsw_comparator: For there our captors asked us for songs, and our tormentors asked for mirth: “Sing for us one of the songs of Zion!”

verses.rationale: Keeps anguished question and territorial estrangement.
verses.before: How can we sing the LORD’s song on foreign soil?
verses.after: How can we sing the LORD’s song on foreign soil?
verses.tsw_comparator: How can we sing the LORD’s song on foreign soil?

verses.rationale: Supplies implied skill without replacing the source's forget verb.
verses.before: If I forget you, Jerusalem, let my right hand forget.
verses.after: If I forget you, Jerusalem, let my right hand forget its skill.
verses.tsw_comparator: If I forget you, Jerusalem, let my right hand forget.

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily self-curse and repeated conditions.
verses.before: Let my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember you, if I do not set Jerusalem above my highest joy.
verses.after: Let my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember you, if I do not place Jerusalem above my greatest joy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember you, if I do not set Jerusalem above my highest joy.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated destructive cry and named participants.
verses.before: Remember, O LORD, against the children of Edom the day of Jerusalem, how they said, “Tear it down! Tear it down! Down to its foundations!”
verses.after: LORD, remember what the Edomites did on Jerusalem’s day, how they said, “Strip it bare! Strip it bare, right down to its foundation!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember, O LORD, against the children of Edom the day of Jerusalem, how they said, “Tear it down! Tear it down! Down to its foundations!”

verses.rationale: Keeps passive devastation reading and retaliatory blessing.
verses.before: Daughter Babylon, doomed to destruction, happy is the one who repays you for what you have done to us.
verses.after: Daughter Babylon, doomed to devastation, happy is the one who repays you for what you did to us.
verses.tsw_comparator: Daughter Babylon, doomed to destruction, happy is the one who repays you for what you have done to us.

verses.rationale: Preserves the actual violent wish against children without euphemism or endorsement.
verses.before: Happy is the one who seizes your little ones and dashes them against the rock.
verses.after: Happy is the one who seizes your little children and smashes them against the rock.
verses.tsw_comparator: Happy is the one who seizes your little ones and dashes them against the rock.

verses.rationale: Preserves title and elohim as gods with alternatives noted.
verses.before: I give you thanks, O LORD, with my whole heart; before the gods I sing your praise;
verses.after: Of David. I will thank you with my whole heart; before the gods I will make music for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I give you thanks, O LORD, with my whole heart; before the gods I sing your praise;

verses.rationale: Keeps the utterance above the name while unpacking name as what it proclaims; literal wording is recorded in the note.
verses.before: I bow down toward your holy temple and give thanks to your name for your steadfast love and your faithfulness, for you have exalted your word above all your name.
verses.after: I will bow toward your holy temple and thank your name for your faithful love and faithfulness, for you have exalted your utterance above all that your name proclaims.
verses.tsw_comparator: I bow down toward your holy temple and give thanks to your name for your steadfast love and your faithfulness, for you have exalted your word above all your name.

verses.rationale: Keeps answered call and inward strengthening.
verses.before: On the day I called, you answered me; you made me bold with strength in my soul.
verses.after: On the day I called, you answered me; you made me bold with strength within.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the day I called, you answered me; you made me bold with strength in my soul.

verses.rationale: Preserves universal kings and divine mouth.
verses.before: All the kings of the earth will give you thanks, O LORD, for they have heard the words of your mouth,
verses.after: All the kings of the earth will thank you, LORD, when they hear the utterances of your mouth.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the kings of the earth shall give you thanks, O LORD, for they have heard the words of your mouth,

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated name and greatness as cause.
verses.before: and they will sing of the ways of the LORD, for great is the glory of the LORD.
verses.after: They will sing of the LORD’s ways, for the LORD’s glory is great.
verses.tsw_comparator: and they shall sing of the ways of the LORD, for great is the glory of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves high/low contrast and distant knowledge.
verses.before: For though the LORD is high, he regards the lowly, but the haughty he knows from afar.
verses.after: Though the LORD is high, he sees the lowly; the proud he knows from far away.
verses.tsw_comparator: For though the LORD is high, he regards the lowly, but the haughty he knows from afar.

verses.rationale: Keeps trouble, anger, and distinct hand clauses.
verses.before: Though I walk among trouble, you preserve my life; you stretch out your hand against the anger of my enemies, and your right hand delivers me.
verses.after: Though I walk amid trouble, you keep me alive. You stretch out your hand against my enemies’ anger, and your right hand saves me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Though I walk in the midst of trouble, you preserve my life; you stretch out your hand against the anger of my enemies, and your right hand delivers me.

verses.rationale: Preserves open-ended completion and dependent final plea.
verses.before: The LORD will fulfill his purpose for me; your steadfast love, O LORD, endures forever. Do not forsake the work of your hands.
verses.after: The LORD will bring to completion what concerns me. LORD, your faithful love lasts forever; do not abandon the work of your hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will fulfill his purpose for me; your steadfast love, O LORD, endures forever. Do not forsake the work of your hands.

verses.rationale: Keeps inline title and searched/known pair.
verses.before: O LORD, you have searched me and known me.
verses.after: For the music director. Of David. A psalm. LORD, you have searched me and known me.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, you have searched me and known me.

verses.rationale: Preserves daily movements and remote understanding.
verses.before: You know when I sit down and when I rise up; you discern my thought from far away.
verses.after: You know when I sit and when I rise; you discern my thoughts from far away.
verses.tsw_comparator: You know when I sit down and when I rise up; you discern my thought from far away.

verses.rationale: Keeps searching/sifting image and both activity states.
verses.before: You search out my path and my lying down, and are acquainted with all my ways.
verses.after: You sift my traveling and my lying down; you are familiar with all my ways.
verses.tsw_comparator: You search out my path and my lying down, and are acquainted with all my ways.

verses.rationale: Preserves pre-speech knowledge and emphatic all.
verses.before: Even before a word is on my tongue, O LORD, you know it altogether.
verses.after: Before a word is on my tongue, you, LORD, already know it all.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even before a word is on my tongue, O LORD, you know it altogether.

verses.rationale: Keeps potentially protective or confining image without deciding its emotion.
verses.before: You hem me in, behind and before, and lay your hand upon me.
verses.after: You hem me in behind and before and lay your hand upon me.
verses.tsw_comparator: You hem me in, behind and before, and lay your hand upon me.

verses.rationale: Follows read form and preserves inaccessible height.
verses.before: Such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is high, I cannot reach it.
verses.after: Such knowledge is too wonderful for me, too high for me to reach.
verses.tsw_comparator: Such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is high, I cannot reach it.

verses.rationale: Keeps spirit and face/presence as parallel terms.
verses.before: Where can I go from your Spirit? Or where can I flee from your presence?
verses.after: Where could I go from your spirit? Where could I flee from your presence?
verses.tsw_comparator: Where can I go from your Spirit? Or where can I flee from your presence?

verses.rationale: Preserves both vertical extremes and explicit Sheol.
verses.before: If I ascend to the heavens, you are there; if I make my bed in Sheol, you are there.
verses.after: If I climb to heaven, you are there; if I make my bed in Sheol, there you are.
verses.tsw_comparator: If I ascend to the heavens, you are there; if I make my bed in Sheol, you are there.

verses.rationale: Keeps east-west poetic travel rather than abstract everywhere.
verses.before: If I take the wings of the morning and dwell at the farthest limits of the sea,
verses.after: If I take the wings of dawn and settle at the farthest edge of the sea,
verses.tsw_comparator: If I take the wings of the morning and dwell at the farthest limits of the sea,

verses.rationale: Preserves guidance and firm grasp separately.
verses.before: even there your hand will lead me, and your right hand will hold me fast.
verses.after: even there your hand will lead me, and your right hand will hold me fast.
verses.tsw_comparator: even there your hand shall lead me, and your right hand shall hold me fast.

verses.rationale: Keeps hypothetical concealment and light's reversal.
verses.before: If I say, “Surely the darkness will cover me, and the light around me become night,”
verses.after: If I say, “Surely darkness will cover me, and the light around me will become night,”
verses.tsw_comparator: If I say, “Surely the darkness shall cover me, and the light around me become night,”

verses.rationale: Preserves threefold reversal of expected concealment.
verses.before: even the darkness is not dark to you; the night is as bright as the day, for darkness is as light to you.
verses.after: even darkness is not dark to you; night shines like day. Darkness and light are alike to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: even the darkness is not dark to you; the night is as bright as the day, for darkness is as light to you.

verses.rationale: Keeps named bodily organ and weaving image with vocabulary support.
verses.before: For it was you who formed my inward parts; you knit me together in my mother’s womb.
verses.after: For you formed my kidneys; you wove me together in my mother’s womb.
verses.tsw_comparator: For it was you who formed my inward parts; you knit me together in my mother’s womb.

verses.rationale: Preserves distinguished/set-apart verb rather than silently replacing it with made.
verses.before: I praise you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Wonderful are your works; my soul knows it well.
verses.after: I thank you because I am awesomely set apart. Your works are wonderful; I know it deep within.
verses.tsw_comparator: I praise you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Wonderful are your works; my soul knows it well.

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily frame and subterranean textile imagery without literalizing location.
verses.before: My frame was not hidden from you when I was being made in secret, intricately woven in the depths of the earth.
verses.after: My frame was not hidden from you when I was made in secret, embroidered in the depths of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: My frame was not hidden from you when I was being made in secret, intricately woven in the depths of the earth.

verses.rationale: Explicitly chooses written negative; divergent read form and syntax recorded in note.
verses.before: Your eyes saw my unformed substance. In your book were written all the days that were formed for me, when none of them as yet existed.
verses.after: Your eyes saw my unformed body. In your book all the days fashioned for me were written, when not one of them yet existed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your eyes saw my unformed substance. In your book were written all the days that were formed for me, when none of them as yet existed.

verses.rationale: Takes thoughts rather than friends and retains numerical vastness.
verses.before: How weighty to me are your thoughts, O God! How vast is the sum of them!
verses.after: How precious your thoughts are to me, God! How vast is their sum!
verses.tsw_comparator: How weighty to me are your thoughts, O God! How vast is the sum of them!

verses.rationale: Preserves sand comparison and waking, without asserting resurrection.
verses.before: If I would count them, they are more than the sand; I awake, and I am still with you.
verses.after: If I counted them, they would outnumber the sand. When I awake, I am still with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: If I would count them, they are more than the sand; I awake, and I am still with you.

verses.rationale: Keeps abrupt death wish and addressed violent men.
verses.before: O that you would slay the wicked, O God, and that the bloodthirsty would depart from me—
verses.after: If only you would kill the wicked, God! You men of bloodshed, leave me!
verses.tsw_comparator: O that you would slay the wicked, O God, and that the bloodthirsty would depart from me—

verses.rationale: Supplies name for compressed taking-in-vain clause with textual difficulty noted.
verses.before: people who speak of you with malicious intent, who lift themselves up against you for evil.
verses.after: They speak of you with evil intent; your enemies take your name in vain.
verses.tsw_comparator: those who speak of you with malicious intent, who lift themselves up against you for evil.

verses.rationale: Preserves hatred and disgust as the speaker's claims.
verses.before: Do I not hate people who hate you, O LORD? And do I not loathe people who rise up against you?
verses.after: Do I not hate those who hate you, LORD, and loathe those who rise against you?
verses.tsw_comparator: Do I not hate those who hate you, O LORD? And do I not loathe those who rise up against you?

verses.rationale: Keeps emphatic total hatred without softening to disagreement.
verses.before: I hate them with perfect hatred; I count them my enemies.
verses.after: I hate them with complete hatred; they have become my enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: I hate them with perfect hatred; I count them my enemies.

verses.rationale: Preserves return to searching and inner anxiety.
verses.before: Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me, and know my thoughts.
verses.after: Search me, God, and know my heart; test me and know my troubling thoughts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me, and know my thoughts.

verses.rationale: Keeps possible painful/idolatrous way ambiguity in note and final guidance plea.
verses.before: See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.
verses.after: See whether there is a hurtful way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.
verses.tsw_comparator: See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.

verses.rationale: Binds separate title and first body record while retaining violent male agents.
verses.before: Deliver me, O LORD, from evil people; preserve me from violent ones,
verses.after: For the music director. A psalm of David. Rescue me, LORD, from evil people; guard me from violent men,
verses.tsw_comparator: Deliver me, O LORD, from evil people; preserve me from violent ones,

verses.rationale: Keeps inward planning and continuous conflict.
verses.before: who devise evils in their hearts and stir up wars all day long.
verses.after: who devise evil in their hearts and stir up battles all day.
verses.tsw_comparator: who devise evils in their hearts and stir up wars all day long.

verses.rationale: Preserves two poisonous speech images and source marker.
verses.before: They sharpen their tongue like a serpent; the venom of a viper is under their lips. Selah.
verses.after: They sharpen their tongues like snakes; viper’s venom is under their lips. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: They sharpen their tongue like a serpent; the venom of a viper is under their lips. Selah.

verses.rationale: Keeps hands, violent men, and deliberate stumbling.
verses.before: Guard me, O LORD, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from violent people, who have planned to trip my steps.
verses.after: Keep me, LORD, from the hands of the wicked; guard me from violent men who plan to trip my steps.
verses.tsw_comparator: Guard me, O LORD, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from violent people, who have planned to trip my steps.

verses.rationale: Preserves multiple hunting devices and marker.
verses.before: The proud have hidden a trap for me; with cords they have spread a net; beside the path they have set snares for me. Selah.
verses.after: The arrogant have hidden a trap and cords for me; they spread a net beside the path and set snares for me. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The proud have hidden a trap for me; with cords they have spread a net; beside the path they have set snares for me. Selah.

verses.rationale: Keeps both LORD occurrences and direct profession.
verses.before: I say to the LORD, “You are my God.” Give ear, O LORD, to the voice of my pleas for mercy.
verses.after: I say to the LORD, “You are my God.” Listen, LORD, to my pleas for mercy.
verses.tsw_comparator: I say to the LORD, “You are my God.” Give ear, O LORD, to the voice of my pleas for mercy.

verses.rationale: Preserves two divine names and protected head.
verses.before: O LORD my Lord, strength of my salvation, you cover my head in the day of battle.
verses.after: LORD, my Lord, strength of my salvation, you shield my head on the day of battle.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD my Lord, strength of my salvation, you cover my head in the day of battle.

verses.rationale: Retains difficult rise clause as consequence and marker.
verses.before: Do not grant, O LORD, the desires of the wicked; do not let their scheme succeed, lest they exalt themselves. Selah.
verses.after: Do not grant the wicked their desires, LORD; do not let their scheme succeed, or they will rise high. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not grant, O LORD, the desires of the wicked; do not let their scheme succeed, lest they exalt themselves. Selah.

verses.rationale: Follows singular read-form verb and retains head-covering reversal.
verses.before: As for the heads of people who surround me, let the trouble spoken by their lips cover them.
verses.after: As for the heads of those surrounding me, let the harm from their lips cover them.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the heads of those who surround me, let the trouble spoken by their lips cover them.

verses.rationale: Follows read-form fall and preserves unnamed he and irreversible punishment.
